duas.title: Moon Sighting Dua
duas.subcategory: Duas to be recited in Ramadan

parts.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلِلْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْيُمْنِ وَالْإِيْمَانِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ رَبِّيْ وَرَبُّكَ اللَّهُ
parts.arabic_alt: اَللّٰهُمَّ اَهْلِلْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْيُمْنِ وَالْاِيْمَانِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ وَالْاِسْلَامِ رَبِّيْ وَرَبُّكَ اللّٰهُ
parts.transliteration: Allaahumma ahlilhu `alaina bil-yumni wal-iman, was-salamati wal-Islam, rabbi wa rabbuk Allah
parts.translation: O Allah, bring it over us with blessing and faith, and safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.
parts.note: Rasulullah (ﷺ) used to say this dua when he saw the new moon. It is masnun to recite this dua after seeing the new moon of Ramadan and all the months.

duas.raw_markdown:
اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلِلْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْيُمْنِ وَالْإِيْمَانِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ رَبِّيْ وَرَبُّكَ اللَّهُ

اَللّٰهُمَّ اَهْلِلْهُ عَلَيْنَا بِالْيُمْنِ وَالْاِيْمَانِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ وَالْاِسْلَامِ رَبِّيْ وَرَبُّكَ اللّٰهُ

Allaahumma ahlilhu `alaina bil-yumni wal-iman, was-salamati wal-Islam, rabbi wa rabbuk Allah

Translation

O Allah, bring it over us with blessing and faith, and safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.

Rasulullah (ﷺ) used to say this dua when he saw the new moon. It is masnun to recite this dua after seeing the new moon of Ramadan and all the months.

ReferenceSahih (Albani). Tirmidhi: 3451

duas.title: Powerful Dua for Travel (Masnun Dua)

parts.intro: Rasulullah (ﷺ) used to say Bismillah while boarding the ride, he said the rest after setting down:
parts.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِيْنَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللّهُ أَكْبَرُ، (لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ) سُبْحَانَكَ، إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِيْ فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوْبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
parts.arabic_alt: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهٗ مُقْرِنِيْنَ وَاِنَّا اِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، (لَا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اَنْتَ) سُبْحَانَكَ، اِنِّيْ ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِيْ فَاغْفِرْ لِيْ فَاِنَّهٗ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوْبَ اِلَّا اَنْتَ
parts.transliteration: Alhamdu lillaah. Subhaanal-ladhee sakhkhara lanaa haadhaa wa maa kunnaa lahu muqrineen. Wa 'innaa 'ilaa Rabbinaa lamunqaliboon. Alhamdu lillaah, alhamdu lillaah, alhamdu lillaah, Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar, (laa ilahaa 'illaa 'Anta) subhaanaka 'innee dhalamtu nafsee faghfir lee, fa'innahu laa yaghfirudh-dhunooba 'illaa 'Anta
parts.translation: All praise is for Allah. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and indeed, to our Lord we will return. All praise is for Allah, all praise is for Allah, all praise is for Allah. Allah is most great, Allah is most great, Allah is most great. (There is no god except You), glory be to You! Indeed, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for indeed, none forgives sins except You.

Rasulullah (ﷺ) used to say Bismillah while boarding the ride, he said the rest after setting down:

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِيْنَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللّهُ أَكْبَرُ، (لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ) سُبْحَانَكَ، إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِيْ فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوْبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ

duas.title: Dua for Journey & Protection (Travel dua)

parts.intro: Abdullah bin Umar (RA) said that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite this dua at the beginning of his journey:
parts.arabic: اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِيْنَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى، اَللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ، اَللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيْفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوْءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ
parts.arabic_alt: اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهٗ مُقْرِنِيْنَ، وَاِنَّا اِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنَّا نَسْاَلُكَ فِيْ سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوٰى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضٰى، اَللّٰهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهٗ، اَللّٰهُمَّ اَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيْفَةُ فِي الْاَهْلِ، اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنِّيْ اَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَّعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَاٰبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوْءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْاَهْلِ
parts.transliteration: Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar. Subhaanal-lathee sakhkhara lanaa haadhaa wa maa kunnaa lahu muqrineen. Wa 'innaa 'ilaa Rabbinaa lamunqaliboon. Allaahumma 'innaa nas'aluka fee safarinaa haadhal-birra wattaqwaa, waminal-'amali maa tardhaa, Allaahumma hawwin 'alaynaa safaranaa haadhaa watwi 'annaa bu'dahu, Allaahumma 'Antas-saahibu fis-safari, walkhaleefatu fil-'ahli, Allaahumma 'innee 'A'oodhu bika min wa'thaa'is-safari, wa ka-'aabatil-mandhari, wa soo'il-munqalabi fil-maali wal 'ahli
parts.translation: Allah is most great, Allah is most great, Allah is most great. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and indeed, to our Lord we will return. O Allah, indeed we ask You in this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and of deeds that which pleases You. O Allah, make easy for us this journey of ours, and fold up for us its distance. O Allah, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over the family. O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, and gloomy sights, and an evil return to wealth and family.

parts.intro: And when the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from his journey, he would recite it and add to it:
parts.arabic: آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
parts.arabic_alt: اٰيِبُوْنَ، تَائِبُوْنَ، عَابِدُوْنَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُوْنَ
parts.transliteration: Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun
parts.translation: We are returning in safety, turning to our Rob, worshipping Him and praising Him.

duas.raw_markdown:
Abdullah bin Umar (RA) said that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite this dua at the beginning of his journey:

اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِيْنَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى، اَللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ، اَللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيْفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوْءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ

اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهٗ مُقْرِنِيْنَ، وَاِنَّا اِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنَّا نَسْاَلُكَ فِيْ سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوٰى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضٰى، اَللّٰهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهٗ، اَللّٰهُمَّ اَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيْفَةُ فِي الْاَهْلِ، اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنِّيْ اَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَّعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَاٰبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوْءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْاَهْلِ

Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar, Allahu 'Akbar. Subhaanal-lathee sakhkhara lanaa haadhaa wa maa kunnaa lahu muqrineen. Wa 'innaa 'ilaa Rabbinaa lamunqaliboon. Allaahumma 'innaa nas'aluka fee safarinaa haadhal-birra wattaqwaa, waminal-'amali maa tardhaa, Allaahumma hawwin 'alaynaa safaranaa haadhaa watwi 'annaa bu'dahu, Allaahumma 'Antas-saahibu fis-safari, walkhaleefatu fil-'ahli, Allaahumma 'innee 'A'oodhu bika min wa'thaa'is-safari, wa ka-'aabatil-mandhari, wa soo'il-munqalabi fil-maali wal 'ahli

Translation

Allah is most great, Allah is most great, Allah is most great. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and indeed, to our Lord we will return. O Allah, indeed we ask You in this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and of deeds that which pleases You. O Allah, make easy for us this journey of ours, and fold up for us its distance. O Allah, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over the family. O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, and gloomy sights, and an evil return to wealth and family.

* * *

And when the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from his journey, he would recite it and add to it:

آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ

اٰيِبُوْنَ، تَائِبُوْنَ، عَابِدُوْنَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُوْنَ

Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun

Translation

We are returning in safety, turning to our Rob, worshipping Him and praising Him.

ReferenceMuslim: 1342

duas.title: Talbiyah For Hajj (Labaik Allahuma Labaik Dua)

parts.arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ، لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
parts.arabic_alt: لَبَّيْكَ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيْكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ، لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيْكَ لَكَ

duas.title: Protection from Jinn Hadith
duas.subcategory: Duas for expelling the devil and his whisperings

parts.intro: 1\. Seek refuge in Allah from Satan; 2\. Give Azan [1] 3\. Remembrance and recitation of the Qur'an; And [2] 4\. Spitting three times on the left during salah and recitation of the Qur'an. Moreover, the other things that drive away the devils are the adhkaar of morning and evening, the adhkaar of sleep, the adhkaar of awakening, the adhkaar of entering and leaving the house, the adhkaar of entering and leaving the mosque, etc., and those adhkaar which are according to the Shari'ah. For example, Ayatul Kursi, the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah during sleep. Moreover, the person who recites "La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu, wahua 'ala qulli shayin qadir" a hundred times, will give him complete protection for that day. Also giving the Azan, Satan fled. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Do not turn your houses into graves. Surely Satan flees from the house where Surah Al-Baqarah is recited." [Muslim: 780]
parts.arabic: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ مَقَابِرَ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَنْفِرُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي تُقْرَأُ فِيهِ سُورَةُ الْبَقَرَةِ
parts.transliteration: Laa taj'aloo buyootakum maqaabira, innash-shaytaana yanfiru minal-baytil-ladhee tuqra'u feehi Sooratul-Baqarah.
parts.translation: Do not make your houses graveyards. Indeed, Satan flees from the house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited.

Moreover, the other things that drive away the devils are the adhkaar of morning and evening, the adhkaar of sleep, the adhkaar of awakening, the adhkaar of entering and leaving the house, the adhkaar of entering and leaving the mosque, etc., and those adhkaar which are according to the Shari'ah. For example, Ayatul Kursi, the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah during sleep. Moreover, the person who recites "La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu, wahua 'ala qulli shayin qadir" a hundred times, will give him complete protection for that day. duas.title: Masnoon dua (Astaghfirullah)
duas.subcategory: Istigfaar which are mentioned in Hadith

parts.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
parts.arabic_alt: اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللّٰهَ
parts.transliteration: astaghfir-ullaah
parts.translation: I ask Allah for forgiveness.

duas.raw_markdown:
أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ

اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللّٰهَ

astaghfir-ullaah

Translation

I ask Allah for forgiveness.

ReferenceBukhari: 6307

duas.title: Masnun Dua (Astaghfirullah Wa Atubu Ilaih)
duas.subcategory: Istigfaar which are mentioned in Hadith

parts.intro: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite more than seventy times a day:
parts.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوْبُ إِلَيْهِ
parts.arabic_alt: اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللّٰهَ وَاَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهِ
parts.transliteration: astaghfir-ullaaha wa atuwb 'iilayhi
parts.translation: I ask Allah for forgiveness and I repent to Him.

duas.raw_markdown:
The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite more than seventy times a day:

أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوْبُ إِلَيْهِ

اَسْتَغْفِرُ اللّٰهَ وَاَتُوْبُ اِلَيْهِ

astaghfir-ullaaha wa atuwb 'iilayhi

Translation

I ask Allah for forgiveness and I repent to Him.

ReferenceBukhari: 6307

parts.intro: Narrated Abdullah ibn Umar (RA): We counted that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say this dua a hundred times during a meeting -
parts.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (الْغَفُوْرُ)
parts.arabic_alt: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِيْ وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ اِنَّكَ اَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيْمُ (الغَفُوْرُ)
parts.transliteration: Rabbighfirli Watub Alayya Innaka Antat-Tawwabul- rahim [in another narration there is al-Ghaffur instead of al-Rahim]
parts.translation: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful (the Forgiving).

duas.title: Khutbah for Nikah (Khutbah al-Hajah)

parts.intro: Abdullah bin Mas'ud (RA) narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us the Tashah-hud for Salat and the Tashah-hud for Al-Hajjah." He said: "The Tashah-hud for Salat is:
parts.arabic: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا، مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَّا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًۭا سَدِيدًا يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا
parts.arabic_alt: اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلّٰهِ نَحْمَدُهٗ وَنَسْتَعِيْنُهٗ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهٗ وَنَعُوْذُ بِاللّٰهِ مِنْ شُرُوْرِ اَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ اَعْمَالِنَا، مَنْ يَّهْدِ اللّٰهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهٗ ـ وَمَنْ يُّضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهٗ ـ اَشْهَدُ اَنْ لَّا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ وَاَشْهَدُ اَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهٗ وَرَسُوْلُهٗ ـ يَا اَيُّهَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهٖ وَلَا تَمُوْتُنَّ اِلَّا وَاَنْتُمْ مُّسْلِمُوْنَ يَا اَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوْا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِيْ خَلَقَكُم مِّنْ نَّفْسٍ وَّاحِدَةٍ ـ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيْرًا وَّنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ الَّذِيْ تَسَاءَلُوْنَ بِهٖ وَالْاَرْحَامَ ۚ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيْبًا يَا اَيُّهَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ وَقُوْلُوْا قَوْلًا سَدِيْدًا يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ اَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوْبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُّطِعِ اللّٰهَ وَرَسُوْلَهٗ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيْمًا
parts.transliteration: Innal-hamda lillaah nahmaduhu wa nasta‛eenuhu wa nastaghfiruhu, wa na‛oodhu billaahi min shuroori anfusinaa wa min sayyi'aati a‛maalinaa, man yahdih-illaahu fa laa mudilla lah, wa man yudlil fa laa haadiya lah, ash-hadu an laa ilaaha ill-Allaahu, wa ash-hadu anna muhammadan ‛abduhu wa rasooluh Yaa ayyuhal-ladheena aamanut-taqullaaha 'haqqa tuqaatihi walaa tamootunna illaa wa antum muslimoon yaa ayyuhan-naasut-taqoo rabbakum-ul-ladhee khalaqakum min nafsin wa'hidatin, wa khalaqa minhaa zawjahaa, wa bath-tha minhumaa rijaalan katheeran wanisaa'-an, wat-taqullaahal-ladhee tasaa'aloona bihi wal ar'haam, inn-Allaaha kaana ‛alaykum raqeebaa Yaa ayyuhal-ladheena aamanut-taqullaaha wa qooloo qawlan sadeeda, yusli'h lakum a‛maalakum wa yaghfir lakum dhunoobakum, wa man yuti‛illaaha wa rasoolahu faqad faaza fawz-an ‛azeemaa
parts.translation: Indeed, all praise is for Allah; we praise Him, we seek His help, and we ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evils of ourselves and from the evil of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is no misguider for him; and whomever He leads astray, there is no guide for him. I bear witness that there is no god except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims. O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever, over you, an Observer. O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice. He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great achievement.
parts.note: Then he would talk about his needs. [4]

duas.reference: [1] Surah Al Imran : 3:102 [2] Sura An-nisa : 4:1 [3] Suah Al-Ahjab: 33:70-71 Sohih(albani) Timiji : 1105

duas.title: Dua for Righteous Family (Marriage Dua)

parts.arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
parts.arabic_alt: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ اَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ اَعْيُنٍ وَّاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِيْنَ اِمَامًا
parts.translation: Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.

duas.raw_markdown:
رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا

رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ اَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ اَعْيُنٍ وَّاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِيْنَ اِمَامًا

Translation

Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous.

ReferenceSurah Furqan 25:74

duas.title: Dua for a Newly Married Couple (Marriage Dua)

parts.arabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِي خَيْرٍ
parts.arabic_alt: بَارَكَ اللّٰهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِيْ خَيْرٍ
parts.transliteration: BaarakAllaahu laka, wa baaraka 'alayka, wa jama'a baynakumaa fee khayr
parts.translation: May Allah bless you, and bless upon you, and unite both of you in goodness.
parts.note: Abu Hurairah (RA) said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say this to congratulate the newlyweds."

duas.raw_markdown:
بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِي خَيْرٍ

بَارَكَ اللّٰهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِيْ خَيْرٍ

BaarakAllaahu laka, wa baaraka 'alayka, wa jama'a baynakumaa fee khayr

Translation

May Allah bless you, and bless upon you, and unite both of you in goodness.

Abu Hurairah (RA) said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say this to congratulate the newlyweds."

ReferenceSahih (Albani). Abu Dawud: 2130

duas.title: Dhikr and Dua after waking up

parts.intro: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when woke up at night, he uttered 10 times:
parts.arabic: اَللَّهُ اَكْبَرُ
parts.arabic_alt: اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ
parts.transliteration: Allahu Akbaar
parts.translation: Allah is the Greatest.

parts.intro: 10 times:
parts.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
parts.arabic_alt: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ
parts.transliteration: Alhamdu lillah
parts.translation: All Praise is for Allah.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What is Ruqyah ?
ruqyah_articles.text: 'Ruqyah ' is the practice of treating illnesses through Qur'anic ayat and invocations as prescribed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It provides a cure for evil eye, magic and physical ailments.The Qur'an offers perfect solace to a believer - both spiritually and physically. Ruqyah should therefore play an essential role in our lives. Allah (ﷻ) says: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْ‌آنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَ‌حْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ Translation: "We send down in the Qur'an that which is a cure and a mercy for the believers." (17:81-2)As well providing a cure, Ruqyah is an excellent way for the believers to build their Iman and reaffirm their tawhid for Allah (ﷻ). Seeking treatment through the Qur'an demonstrates complete belief in the Book of Allah (ﷻ).The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make good use of the two cures: honey and the Qur'an." (Ibn Majah)'A'ishah (RA) said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ill, Jibril ('alayhis-salam) performed Ruqyah on him." (Muslim)In another hadith, 'A'ishah (RA) informs us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her and found a woman treating her with Ruqyah (through other than the words of Allah (ﷻ)). He (ﷺ) said: "Treat her with the book of Allah (ﷻ)." (Ibn Hibban)She also said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to command me to perform Ruqyah from the evil eye." (Muslim)Upon another occasion, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a girl whose face had changed colour in the house of Umm Salamah (RA), so he (ﷺ) said: "Seek Ruqyah for her, because she has been affected by the evil eye." (Bukhari)'A'ishah (RA) also narrated that whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would become sick, he would recite [the last 3 Surahs of the Qur'an] and then blow over his body.She says: "During his last illness from which he passed away, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to blow over himself. But when his sickness intensified, I used to (recite and then) blow over him using his own hands because of their blessings." (Bukhari)In another hadith, she mentions that whenever anyone from his family would become ill, he (ﷺ) would blow over them with these three Surahs. (Muslim)The Ruqyah that is acceptable in the Sharee'ah is that which fulfills three conditions:1. The Ruqyah must be done with the Quran, with the Names and Attributes of Allaah The Almighty, or with a supplication reported on the authority of the Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhi wa sallam.2. The Ruqyah must be composed of comprehensive Arabic words because it is not appropriate to use a language other than Arabic in supplication. It is only permissible for those who are not fluent in Arabic. Using foreign words in Ruqyah is unacceptable. This was stated by Shaykh Al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allaah have mercy upon him.3. It must be known that Ruqyah has no effect on its own, but it is effective only by the will of Allaah The Almighty.Once these three conditions are fulfilled, it becomes a valid Ruqyah. The Prophet, sallallaahu 'alayhi wa sallam, mentioned that Ruqyah is permissible, provided that it does not include any of the features of Shirk (polytheism). [Muslim]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: The Method Of Ruqyah
ruqyah_articles.text: The 3 RequirementsThere are many actions and incantations associated with Ruqyah which are not valid and contradict the teachings of the Shari'ah.Ibn Hajar (ra) outlined three principles for Ruqyah, which must be adhered to in order for Ruqyah to be valid. They are:The Ruqyah must be with Allah's words or His Names and Attributes.The Ruqyah should be in Arabic or of an understandable meaning (You shouldn't write or say something which is illegible or obscure).You should believe that they do not have an effect in of themselves, but rather the effect of the Ruqyah only occurs by the will of Allah. (Fath al-Bari)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Conditions for Ruqyah to be successful
ruqyah_articles.text:
IntentionRuqyah is a du'a. The intention should always be to ask Allah to remove the evil by the words of the Qur'an.

* * *

Conviction (yaqin)One should recite loudly and clearly, with firm conviction and belief in Allah, who Alone gives cure.

* * *

Patience & ConsistencyLike all treatment, consistency is key. Daily recitation, du'a' and other treatments must be maintained for positive results.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Before Ruqyah
ruqyah_articles.text: Make wuḍu, offer two rak'ats and make sincere du'a'. Du'a', especially in tahajjud, brings great reprieve and assistance from Allah (ﷻ).Make abundant and sincere istighfar (seeking forgiveness from Allah ﷻ), and stay away from sins. One should restore people's rights if they have wronged anyone or taken anything unjustly.Give Sadaqah as it wards off calamity (Bayhaqi). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Treat your sick by giving Sadaqah." (Bayhaqi)Remove animate pictures from the home. Any amulets (ta'widh) which contain illegible text or invokes upon other than Allah should also be taken out and disposed of in a river.Remain in a state of wuḍu through the day and also sleep with wuḍu.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: During Ruqyah
ruqyah_articles.text: Begin Ruqyah by sending Salawat (salutations) upon the Prophet (ﷺ). Recite the Ruqyah loudly, clearly and with concentration, at least 3 or 7 times.One may recite directly into the hands, blowing into them and rubbing them over the body. One can also recite whilst placing the hands over the part of the body that is in pain.One may recite and blow on water. Keep the mouth close to the water, breathe into it and repeatedly blow over it. This can be used for drinking and bathing. Olive oil and other Sunnah medicines can be recited upon and applied to the body.When reciting on others, place the hand on the forehead of the affected person (mahram only), or on the part of the body in pain, recite and blow.If one cannot recite, then Ruqyah can be listened to. This should be done with full concentration. One should listen carefully and ensure that they do not fall asleep.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Why Blow with Your Saliva?
ruqyah_articles.text: Ruqyah comes from the heart and mouth of the reciter, so if it is accompanied with some of his saliva and breath, that will maximise the strength and effectiveness of the remedy. The stronger the heart of the person is, the stronger the Ruqyah he recites becomes.Combining both Ruqyah (from the heart and mouth) and spitting with one's saliva (aspects of the inner self) form a powerful antidote to the evil of the magicians and devils.There is another secret behind blowing when performing Ruqyah : blowing is done by both pure and evil souls, as Allah said: وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ﴿٤﴾ Translation: "And from the evil of the blowers in knots." (113:4)Those who do magic tie knots and blow onto them words of magic, mixing them with their saliva which work on the victims even in their absence. However, the pure souls counter this by blowing with the powerful words of the Almighty. (Adapted from Zad al-Ma'ad)'If one's faith, soul, and spirit are strong, and if he internalises the meaning and essence of Surah al-Fatihah, recites it and then blows on the affected person followed by his spittle, this will counter the effects incurred by evil beings. And Allah knows best.' (Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma'ad)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Blowing in Water
ruqyah_articles.text: One may pray and blow into water as a form of remedy. In the authentic narration of Muṣannaf ibn Abi Shaybah, 'A'ishah (RA) permitted that water can be prayed on and then given to the sick to drink or to be poured over them.Salih (rahimahullah), the son of Imam Ahmad (rahimahullah), said: "Whenever I became ill, my father would take a cup of water and recite over it, then tell me to drink some of it and wash my hands and face in it." (Manaqib al-Imam Ahmad)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: FAQ's About Ruqya
ruqyah_articles.text:
Can anyone do Ruqyah or is it only for certain people?There is a misconception that Ruqyah is exclusive to certain individuals.Ruqyah can and should be performed by every Muslim.

* * *

Is reciting Ruqyah better than listening to it?One should recite themselves if they can do so in the proper manner. However Ruqyah may need to be done for long periods of time and one may be unable to recite for such durations. One can therefore listen to a Ruqyah audio or have someone recite over them.

* * *

How long should the Ruqyah be recited or listened to?Listen to Ruqyah for a few hours a day. Ideally one should stop other activities and focus on the Ruqyah until they get better. This may take a several days or even longer depending on the severity of the illness/magic/evil eye.

* * *

Reciting or listening to the Ruqyah is not making a difference.If reciting or listening to Ruqyah is not making a difference, then one should question their yaqin (conviction) and niyyah (intention). One should also do istighfar (seek forgiveness from Allah ﷻ) as there may be a sin which is preventing Allah's (ﷻ) help. Istighfar opens all closed doors.

* * *

How does one know if they're afflicted with evil eye, etc?The best gauge for knowing whether one is afflicted is the Qur'an. Nothing can hide from the powerful and supreme words of the Almighty (ﷻ).One may feel pain while reciting or listening to Ruqyah. One may also feel restless or scared. Other symptoms may include itching, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, sweating, an urge to urinate or feeling sleepy. If these symptoms arise, continue reciting or listening to Ruqyah, especially the ayat that exacerbate these symptoms.

* * *

The person afflicted refuses to recite or listen to the Ruqyah.One who does not want to listen to Ruqyah should be compelled as the shaytan is stopping them from seeking treatment. If it's still difficult, then one can recite on their behalf and blow on water and oil. The afflicted person should be made to drink and use these.

* * *

Should illnesses be treated with Ruqyah only?Magic and evil eye can often cause physical illnesses. These need to be treated medically alongside the Ruqyah. Along with conventional medicine, one should adopt a healthy lifestyle and implement the sunnah prescription of eating less but more wholesome foods. Our consumption and the means to obtain it should also be halal. After Ruqyah, one may feel weak. Eating foods which are high in energy, including Talbinah (barley porridge) is therefore helpful.

* * *

Are there specific ayat in the Qur'an that have more impact?The Qur'an has many ayat of Ruqyah. The strongest are Surah al-Fatihah, Ayah al-Kursi and the last 3 Surahs of the Qur'an. Listen to these for hours if possible. If certain ayat elicit greater symptoms, then these should be repeated at least 7 times if possible. One can also add other verses which mention the Greatness and the Oneness of Allah such as 2:164, 3:18, 7:54, 23:118, 72:3, 37:1-10, 59:24, Surah al-Mulk and al-Rahman.

* * *

Do the Sunnah morning and evening adhkar help?The morning and evening adhkar (Sunnah remembrances after Fajr and 'Asr) are the best means of safeguarding oneself from evil eye, magic and other afflictions. If someone is already afflicted, then these adhkar should also be read along with the Ruqyah treatment.The morning and evening adhkar are highly important and should never be abandoned. One who is cured by Ruqyah will always remain exposed to evil afflictions if they neglect these adhkar.

* * *

Why should one blow after reciting Ruqyah ?Blowing with the saliva is an important part of the Ruqyah. This physical element should not be underestimated, as Ibn al-Qayyim (rahimahullah) explains in Zad al-Ma'ad. "Blowing is done by both pure and evil souls, as Allah (ﷻ) said: 'And from the evil of the blowers in knots.' (113:4)Those who do magic tie knots and blow onto them words of magic, mixing them with their saliva which work on the victims even in their absence. However, the pure souls counter this by blowing with the powerful words of the Almighty (ﷻ). This is because the pure souls and the majestic words of the Almighty (ﷻ) clash with and destroy the 'evil' from the evil souls (whether they are magicians, evil jinns or enviers)."

* * *

What is a Ruqyah bath?A Ruqyah bath is where one bathes in water that has been recited upon. Whilst reciting Ruqyah over the water, one should keep their mouth close to the water, breathe into the water and repeatedly blow over it. Baths should be done daily for positive results. For more severe afflictions, daily baths should continue until symptoms subside.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Prerequisites of writing Ruqyah and drinking it's water
ruqyah_articles.text: Scholars have varying opinions regarding the permissibility of writing verses from the Quran on a piece of paper, tablet, dish or vessel and then washing it with water and giving this water to the patient to drink as a remedy. Some of them considered it an innovation in religion, such as the Maaliki scholar Ibn Al-'Arabi, may Allaah have mercy upon him, whereas some of the righteous predecessors held that it was permissible and they quoted a narration on the authority of Ibn 'Abbaas, may Allaah be pleased with him.In this regard, the Hanbali scholar, Ibn Al-Qayyim, may Allaah have mercy upon him, mentioned on the authority of Mujaahid and Abu Qilaabah, may Allaah have mercy upon them, that a group of the righteous predecessors were of the view that it was permissible to write verses from the Quran, wash them with water and then let the patient drink it. Another scholar supporting this view was the Shaafi'i scholar, An-Nawawi, may Allaah have mercy upon him. He mentioned that Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Mujaahid, Abu Qilaabah and Al-Awzaa'i, may Allaah have mercy upon them, held that it was permissible, whereas An-Nakha'i, may Allaah have mercy upon him, considered it to be disliked. An-Nawawi, may Allaah have mercy upon him, added that it was permissible according to the requisites of the Shaafi'i School of Fiqh, and that Al-Qaadhi Husayn, Al-Baghawi and others, may Allaah have mercy upon them, held it to be permissible.Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allaah have mercy upon him, quoted the view of Ahmad, may Allaah have mercy upon him, and mentioned that it was permissible to write some verses from the Quran using permissible ink and wash them with water and then let the patient drink it. Referring to this, 'Abdullaah ibn Ahmad, may Allaah have mercy upon him, reported on the authority of his father (i.e. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allaah have mercy upon him) that Ibn 'Abbaas, may Allaah be pleased with him, said that when a woman faces difficulty in childbirth, the following may be written for her: بِسْمِ اللهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ الْحَلِيْمُ الْكَرِيْمُ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيْمِ، اَلْحَمْد للهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِيْنَ Transliteration: "Bismillaah. Laa ilaaha illa Allaah Al-Haleem Al-Kareem. Subhaanallaah Rabil-'Arsh Al-'Atheem. Al-Hamdulillaahi Rabil-'Aalameen.Translation: In the name of Allaah, none is worthy of worship but Allaah, the Forbearing the Generous. Exalted is Allaah the Lord of the Great Throne. All perfect praise be to Allaah, The Lord of the worlds. كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا ﴿٤٦﴾ Translation: It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof. [Quran 79: 46] فَاصْبِرْ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُولُو الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلَا تَسْتَعْجِل لَّهُمْ ۚ كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا سَاعَةً مِّن نَّهَارٍ ۚ بَلَاغٌ ۚ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ ﴿٣٥﴾ Translation: On the Day they see that which they are promised - as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people? [Quran 46: 35]He, may Allaah have mercy upon him, also reported on the authority of his father, may Allaah have mercy upon him, that it was permissible to write verses from the Quran on a clean vessel, wash it with water and let the patient drink it. Wakee', may Allaah have mercy upon him, added to the narration of Ibn 'Abbaas, may Allaah be pleased with him, that the woman drinks from the water and the part of her body below the navel is sprinkled with it.Consequently, we see that it is permissible to do this when the following prerequisites are satisfied: Using pure ink when writing the Quran and writing it on a pure object. One should not write the verses with blood, as some ignorant people do, because blood is impure and the Book of Allaah and His verses are not to be exposed to impurities.The Hanbali scholar, Ibn Muflih , may Allaah have mercy upon him, mentioned that Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allaah have mercy upon him, used to write on the forehead of the patient in cases of nosebleeding:  وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ وَيَا سَمَاءُ أَقْلِعِي وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ ۖ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ ﴿٤٤﴾ Translation: And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished. [Quran 11: 44] Ibn Muflih, may Allaah have mercy upon him, added that it was not permissible to write it with blood because blood is impure and the words of Allaah The Almighty must not be written with it.Furthermore, it is better to drink the water than use it to perform Ghusl (ritual bathing). It was reported on the authority of Imaam Ahmad, may Allaah have mercy upon him, that it was disliked to use this water to perform Ghusl. The Hanbali Scholar, Ibn Muflih, may Allaah have mercy upon him, mentioned that Al-Khallaal, may Allaah have mercy upon him, explained that the reason behind this ruling was that the water used in Ghusl moves in sewers in dirty places, therefore, Quranic water must be safeguarded from this, whereas drinking it is not disliked since it is therapeutic.Another prerequisite is that the written item must be from the Quran, Athkaar (remembrances and mentionings of Allaah) or comprehensible supplications. Using talismans, polytheistic spells or incomprehensible words are not permissible. It was reported on the authority of 'Awf ibn Maalik, may Allaah be pleased with him, that he asked the Prophet, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, about the Ruqyah s of the pre-Islamic era, and the Prophet, sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam, answered that they were permissible as long as they did not include any form of polytheism. [Muslim and Abu Daawood]Quoting this Hadeeth, Ash-Shawkaani, may Allaah have mercy upon him, mentioned that it was permissible to make Ruqyah and seek remedy with things that bring no harm and do not contradict the Sharee'ah, even if they are not the Names of Allaah The Almighty or verses of the Quran. However, they must be comprehensible; otherwise, they might include polytheism.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: The correct way to perform Ruqyah for a small child
ruqyah_articles.text: The correct way to perform Ruqyah for a small child in order to protect him is what the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do for his (grand) sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them).Al-Bukhaari (3371) narrated that Ibn 'Abbaas (RA) said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge with Allah for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and he said: "Your father (Ibraaheem) used to seek refuge with (these words) for Ismaa'eel and Ishaaq: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ Transliteration: A'oodhu bi kalimaat Illaahi't-taammah min kulli shaytaanin wa haammah wa min kulli 'aynin laammah.Translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allaah from every devil and every vermin, and from every bad eye. Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Baari (6/410):The word "haammah (vermin)" refers to poisonous things.The words "from every bad eye" - al-Khattaabi (R) said: What is meant by this is every disease and ailment that may affect a person of insanity and confusion. End quote. It is also mustahabb when performing Ruqyah for children to recite al-Mu'awwidhatayn (the last two soorahs of the Qur'an) over them and to wipe their bodies whilst reciting, or to recite them into one's hands and blow in them, spitting lightly, then wipe them over whatever of their body one can reach, or to recite them into water and wipe them or wash them with it. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for himself and others by means of these two soorahs.It was narrated that Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri (RA) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge with Allah from the jinn and people's eyes (i.e., the evil eye) until the Mu'aawidhatayn were revealed, then when they were revealed he began to recite them for protection and stopped reciting anything else.Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2058); classed as saheeh by al-Albaani in Saheeh at-Tirmidhi.Blowing with a little saliva after reciting the Mu'aawidhatayn is taken from the practice of the Prophet (ﷺ) just before going to sleep. He used to recite them into his hands and blow into them, then wipe his body with his hands. When he fell sick, 'Aa'ishah used to do that for him, which indicates that in the case of a small child, his mother can recite the Mu'aawidhatayn and blow (into her hands) and wipe his body with them.It was narrated that 'Aa'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to his bed, he would blow into his hands after reciting Qul Huwa Allaahu Ahad (Soorat al-Ikhlaas) and the Mu'aawidhatayn, then he would wipe his face and whatever he could reach of his body with his hands. 'Aa'ishah said: And when he fell sick, he would tell me to do that for him. Narrated by al-Bukhaari (5748). With regard to the adkhaar for the morning and evening, there is no report - as far as we know - to suggest that they may be recited over others with the intention of performing Ruqyah, so we do not advise you to carry on doing that; rather you should limit it to what has been proven from the Prophet (ﷺ), for that is sufficient. The best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ).

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Are physical medicines better, or Ruqyah and spiritual medicine?
ruqyah_articles.text: There is no doubt that man suffers psychological diseases, such as anxiety about the future and grief for the past. Psychological diseases may have a greater impact on the body than physical diseases. Treating these diseases by means of something prescribed in sharee'ah - i.e., Ruqyah - is more successful than treating them by means of physical medicines, as is well known.Among the means of treating them: the saheeh haseeth narrated from Ibn Mas'ood (may Allaah be pleased with him): "There is no believer who is stricken by anxiety, distress or grief, and he says, 'Allaahumma inni 'abduka ibnu 'abdika ibnu amatika, naasiyati bi yadika, maadin fiyya hukmuka, 'adlun fiyya qadaa'uka, as'aluka bi kulli ismin huwa laka sammayta bihi nafsaka aw 'allamtahu ahadan min khalqika aw anzaltahu fi kitaabika aw asta'tharta bihi fi 'ilm il-ghaybi 'indaka an taj'ala al-Qur'aan al-'azeem rabee'a qalbi wa noora sadri wa jalaa'a huzni wa dhahaaba hammi wa ghammi (O Allaah, I am Your slave, son of Your slave, son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your command over me is forever executed and Your decree over me is just. I ask You by every name belonging to You which You have named Yourself with, or taught to any of Your creation, or revealed in Your Book, or You have preserved in the knowledge of the Unseen with You, that You make the Holy Qur'aan the life of my heart and the light of my breast, and a departure for my sorrow and a release for my anxiety and distress)', but Allaah will relieve him." This is one of the medicines prescribed in sharee'ah.Similarly, one may say,  لَّا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ Translation: none has the right to be worshipped but You (O Allaah), Glorified (and Exalted) be You [above all that (evil) they associate with You]! Truly, I have been of the wrongdoers. [cf. al-Anbiyaa' 21:87]If you want to know more, please refer to the writings of the scholars on the topic of adhkaar (dhikr, remembering Allaah), such as al-Waabil al-Sayyib by Ibn al-Qayyim, al-Kalim al-Tayyib by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, al-Adhkaar by al-Nawawi, and Zaad al-Ma'aad, by Ibn al-Qayyim.But when faith grows weak, the soul's acceptance of remedies prescribed in sharee'ah also grows weak. People nowadays have begun to rely on physical medicines more than on the spiritual remedies prescribed in Islam. But when faith is strong, the spiritual remedies prescribed in Islam have a more complete effect; their effect may be faster than that of physical medicines. We are all aware of the story of the man whom the Messenger SAWS (ﷺ) sent on a campaign. He camped near some Arabs, but those people near whom he camped did not show him any hospitality. Allaah willed that their chief should be stung by a snake, and they said to one another, "Go to those people who are camped (near us), maybe you will find a raaqi (one who recites Ruqyah, i.e., incantations or prayers for healing) with them." The Sahaabah said to them, "We will not recite Ruqyah for your chief until you give us such and such number of sheep." They said, "We agree." Then one of the Sahaabah went and recited over the one who had been stung; he recited Soorat al-Faatihah only, then that person who had been stung got up as if he was released from a chain. This recitation of al-Faatihah had such an effect in this man because it came from a heart that was filled with faith. When they came back, the Prophet SAWS (ﷺ) said, "How did you know that it is a Ruqyah ?"But in our own times there is this weakness of religious commitment and faith, and people have started to rely on outward physical matters, and this is causing them further suffering.On the other hand there are those who cheat people and deceive them, claiming to be pious reciters of Qur'aan, but they consume people's wealth unlawfully. People are of two extremes, one which thinks that recitation of Qur'aan has no effect at all, and the other extreme composed of cheaters who deceive people by reciting devious recitations, and some are moderate. [Shaykh Ibn 'Uthaymeen, Fataawa Islamiyyah, 4/465, 466 ]But as there is no contradiction between using permissible physical medicines as prescribed by doctors and using spiritual medicines such as Ruqyah and seeking refuge with Allaah and other du'aa's that are proven in sound reports, the two may be combined, as the Prophet SAWS (ﷺ) did. It was proven that he used both kinds of treatment, and he said, "Strive to pursue that which will benefit you and seek refuge with Allaah, and do not feel helpless." And he said: "Seek treatment, O slaves of Allaah, but do not seek treatment with things which are haraam."

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Is Ruqyah?
ruqyah_articles.text: When a person, placing full trust in Allah in the hope of cure from physical, mental, or spiritual illnesses, or from jinn, sihr (magic), and the evil eye ('ayn), etc., recites the Qur'an himself or someone else recites it to him, we call this Shar'i Ruqyah. Shar'i Ruqyah includes not only the Qur'an, but also the du'as mentioned in the hadith. Considering the literal meaning of ruqyah, the raqi can recite ruqyah and blow over the patient, or there is no problem even if he does not blow over.Just as Islam has advised curing illnesses through observing health guidelines and taking medicine and a proper diet, similarly in certain special cases it has also granted permission to cure illness with the help of reciting du'a or incantations. In cases where medicine and diet are of no benefit, especially in those cases there is no objection to seeking treatment through blowing/incantation; rather, in those cases seeking treatment through blowing/incantation is desirable or more suitable.However, what is memorable and noteworthy in this context is that the words of the du'a or incantation must not contain anything contrary to the Shari'ah. Such as magical spells, words of shirk, observing Shari'ah-forbidden dates and moments according to the dictates of astrology, etc. Islam has not recognized these; rather, they have been declared strictly forbidden and haram. Try to understand the following hadith:Hadrat 'Awf bin Malik (RA) says that we used to recite incantations in the age of Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance). So after being initiated into the religion of Islam, we asked, 'O Messenger of Allah! What is your opinion regarding those incantations?'The Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'Present your incantations to me. As long as there are no words of shirk in them, I have no objection to using them.' (Sahih Muslim, Mishkat p. 88)Therefore, any du'a or incantation that does not contain the names of gods and goddesses, jinn and ghosts, or any pir or wali, or any words seeking help from them, there is no fault in reciting such incantations. On the other hand, it is also necessary to stay away from reciting incantations whose meaning is not understandable, out of fear that there might perhaps be something forbidden in them.On the other hand, there is no prohibition against using those incantations that contain no forbidden words. The proof of this lies in the following two hadiths:1. 'A'ishah (RA) says that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to recite incantations and blow (perform ruqyah) in order to remove the evil effects of the evil eye. (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Mishkat p. 388)2. Hadrat Anas (RA) says, "The Messenger of Allah permitted blowing (ruqyah) for curing the evil eye, poisonous stings, and infected sores." (Sahih Muslim, Mishkat p. 388)Help from reciting du'a and incantations may be taken in all kinds of illnesses and diseases. But reciting incantations is more effective in the case of the above three afflictions compared to other illnesses, and because the benefits of reciting incantations are observed more prominently, these three have been specifically mentioned in the hadith.Writing du'a and incantations, washing them off, and drinking that water, or reciting incantations and blowing (performing ruqyah) is not unlawful; rather, it is something supported by the hadith. But writing them as a ta'weez (amulet) and hanging it on the arm or around the neck is not right. Take note of a hadith regarding this:Hadrat Zaynab (RA), the wife of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA), says, once seeing a thread hanging around my neck, 'Abdullah said, 'What is this around your neck?' I said, 'This is a thread; an incantation has been recited over it.' Hearing this, 'Abdullah grabbed the thread and tore it off, saying, 'The family of 'Abdullah has thus far kept free from shirk, and what is this of yours? This falls into the category of shirk! I heard with my own ears from the Noble Prophet (ﷺ). He said, "Forbidden du'as and incantations, hanging amulets on hands or necks, and magic spells--all of these are included in shirk."' (Sunan Abi Dawud, Mishkat p. 389)The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) says, "Using amulets, bangles, iron bracelets, etc., brings no benefit whatsoever; rather, it only brings harm." (Musnad Ahmad 4:45, Sunan Ibn Majah 3531)All amulets that are written with numbers by drawing diagrams, made with the names of any angel, jinn, or Shaytan, or with the help of talismanic magic, or made from any metal, bones, hair, or feathers of animals and birds, or tree roots--using them is undoubtedly shirk.Of course, regarding amulets written with Qur'anic verses, there is a difference of opinion among the scholars. However, not using them either is what is correct. Because,Firstly: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared the use of amulets to be shirk. In that, all types of amulets may be intended.Secondly: The person wearing an amulet written with Qur'anic verses will urinate and defecate, engage in marital intimacy, and women will wear it during menstruation and other states of impurity, while keeping it tied around the neck, arm, or waist. This will cause disrespect and dishonor to the Glorious Qur'an. It is astonishing that according to them, if one enters a threshing room or confinement room wearing an amulet, the amulet becomes defiled. But how does this amulet not become defiled on an impure person?Thirdly: If the use of such amulets is made permissible, then non-Qur'anic amulets will also be seen in use. Therefore, with the intention of uprooting this shirk and closing its loopholes, the use of Qur'anic amulets will also be impermissible.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ruqyahs Mentioned in the Sunnah
ruqyah_articles.text:
IntroductionThere are some du'as and verses narrated in the authentic Sunnah. Such as:أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ السَّمِيْعِ الْعَلِيْمِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ مِنْ هَمْزِهِ وَنَفْخِهِ وَنَفْثِهِTransliteration: A'oodhu billaahis-samee'il-'aleemi minash-shaytaanir-rajeemi min hamzihi wa nafkhihi wa nafthihTranslation: I seek refuge with Allah Ta'ala, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Shaytan and from his evil whispers, his blowing, and his magic spells. [The hadith is sahih. Sunan Abi Dawud: 775, 764; Jami' at-Tirmidhi: 242]Say 3 times,بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِيْ لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُTransliteration: Bismillaahil-ladhee laa yadurru ma'asmihee shay'un fil-ardi wa laa fis-samaa'i, wa huwas-samee'ul-'aleem.Translation: In the name of Allah; with Whose name nothing in the earth or in the heaven can cause harm. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." [Sunan Abi Dawud, 4/323, no. 5088; Jami' at-Tirmidhi, 5/465, no. 3388]اَللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ اِشْفِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِيْ لَا شِفَاءَ إِلاَّ شِفَاؤُكَ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًاTransliteration: Allaahumma rabban-naas, adh-hibil-ba's, ishfi, wa antash-shaafee, laa shifaa'a illaa shifaa'uk, shifaa'an laa yughaadiru saqamaa.Translation: O Allah, O Lord of mankind, remove the distress, grant cure, You are the Healer (the Grantor of cure), there is no cure except Your cure (granting recovery or curing disease), grant a cure after which no sickness or disease remains. [Sahih al-Bukhari: 5743]Say 7 times,أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ رَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَTransliteration: As'alullaahal-'adheem, rabbal-'arshil-'adheem, ay-yashfiyakTranslation: I ask the Magnificent Allah, the Lord of the Mighty Throne, that He grant you cure from illness. [Jami' at-Tirmidhi, no. 2083; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3106]Surah Al-Fatihah, Surah Al-Falaq, Surah An-Nas, etc.The Du'a of Hadrat Ibrahim (AS)-أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍTransliteration: A'oodhu bikalimaatillaahit-taammaati min kulli shaytaaniw-wa haammah, wa min kulli 'aynil-laammah.Translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every shaytan, from all harmful insects and creatures, and from every harmful eye. [Sahih al-Bukhari: 3371]

* * *

Performing Ruqyah by Placing the Hand on the Patient's Affected Limb"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'Place your hand over the place on your body where you feel pain, andsay 3 times,بِسْمِ اللّٰهِTransliteration: BismillaahTranslation: In the name of AllahThen say 7 times, أَعُوْذُ بِاللّٰهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُTransliteration: A'oodhu billaahi wa qudratihee min sharri maa ajidu wa uhaadhirTranslation: I seek refuge in Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and fear. [Sahih Muslim: 222, Jami' at-Tirmidhi: 3588]

* * *

Blowing After RecitationNarrated from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubaydah (RA): He said, once seeing a scar on the shin of Salamah (RA), I asked, 'What is this?' He said, 'I was wounded here in the Battle of Khaybar. People began to say that Salamah has been injured. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought to me and he blew three times onto my wound. As a result, until today I do not feel any pain in it.' [Sunan Abi Dawud (Sahih): 3894]

* * *

Blowing After Reciting Surah Al-Fatihah"A group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once went on a journey. Eventually, they arrived at one of the Arab tribes and wanted to be guests of the tribe. But that tribe refused to host them. Coincidentally, the chief of that tribe was bitten by a snake. They made every effort to cure him, but to no avail. Then someone among them said: If you were to go to that group who came among you, perhaps someone among them might have some remedy.Then they came to that group and said, 'O people of the group! Our chief has been bitten by a snake. We have tried everything for him, but to no avail. Does anyone among you have any remedy?' One of them said, 'Yes. By Allah, I know how to perform ruqyah. But by Allah! We wanted to be your guests, but you did not host us. So I will not perform ruqyah until you fix a wage for us.'Then they agreed to give a flock of goats. Then that Companion went there and kept reciting 'Alhamdulillahi Rabbil 'Alameen' (Surah Al-Fatihah) and blowing. Finally, that person became so well as if he was freed from bonds. He began walking around, as if he had no illness at all. The narrator says: Then they paid the wage that they had fixed. After that, one of the Companions said: Distribute these. At this, the one who had performed the ruqyah said: Do not distribute them until we go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), relate these events to him, and see what he commands us.Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and related the incident. He said, 'How did you know that ruqyah could be performed with it? You have done the right thing. Distribute them, and along with that, allocate a share for me as well.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari (Islamic Foundation): 5338]

* * *

Reciting Du'a by Touching the Earth with a Finger, Then Applying It to the Affected AreaNarrated from 'A'ishah (RA): She said, whenever any person felt pain in any part of their body, or had a boil or an ulcer, or was injured, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) would rub his finger over that place and say,بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ تُرْبَةُ أَرْضِنَا بِرِيقَةِ بَعْضِنَا لِيُشْفَىِ سَقِيمُنَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَاTransliteration: Bismillaah. Turbatu ardinaa, bireeqati ba'dinaa, li-yushfaa saqeemunaa, bi'idhni rabbinaaTranslation: In the name of Allah, the soil of our earth (mixed) with the saliva of one of us, by the command of our Lord, with it, for the purpose of granting cure to our sick person (rubbing this)" [Mishkat al-Masabih (Sahih): 1531]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: How to Take a Ruqyah Bath
ruqyah_articles.text:
IntroductionBathing with recited-upon water is called a ruqyah bath. To prepare the water for a ruqyah bath, one must recite with one's mouth close to the water. While reciting, one should blow every so often (with a slight sprinkling of spittle). If a ruqyah bath is taken every day, then insha-Allah positive results will be obtained. If the illness is severe, then the ruqyah bath should be continued regularly until recovery.

* * *

How to Take a Ruqyah Bath?Shaykh Abdul Aziz bin Baz (rahimahullah) has described the method of bathing. Namely:1. Surah Al-Fatihah2. Ayatul Kursi3. Verses 106-122 of Surah Al-A'raf4. Verses 79-82 of Surah Yunus5. Verses 65-69 of Surah Ta-Ha6. Surah Al-Kafirun7. Surah Al-Ikhlas [3 times]8. Surah Al-Falaq [3 times]9. Surah An-Nas [3 times]Along with some du'as, such as-Say 3 times,اَللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ اِشْفِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِيْ لَا شِفَاءَ إِلاَّ شِفَاؤُكَ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًاTransliteration: Allaahumma rabban-naas, adh-hibil-ba's, ishfi, wa antash-shaafee, laa shifaa'a illaa shifaa'uk, shifaa'an laa yughaadiru saqamaa.Translation: O Allah, O Lord of mankind, remove the distress, grant cure, You are the Healer (the Grantor of cure), there is no cure except Your cure (granting recovery or curing disease), grant a cure after which no sickness or disease remains. [Sahih al-Bukhari: 5743]Say 3 times,بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ أَرْقِيْكَ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيْكَ، مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ، اللّٰهُ يَشْفِيْكَ، بِاسْمِ اللّٰهِ أَرْقِيْكَ.Transliteration: Bismillaahi arqeek, min kulli shay'in yu'dheek, min sharri kulli nafsin aw 'aynin haasidin, Allaahu yashfeek, Bismillaahi arqeekTranslation: In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah on you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul and envious eye, Allah will cure you, in the name of Allah I perform ruqyah on you. [Sahih Muslim: 2186]One should recite the above-mentioned verses and du'as and blow over the patient afflicted with magic or into water taken in a vessel. After that, the person afflicted with magic will drink from that water, and bathe with the remaining water. If this is done once or more as needed, by the will of Allah the patient will be cured. [Majmu' al-Fatawa li-Ibn Baz; 8/144]Do not heat the ruqyah water or mix other water into it. It is hoped that the magic will be broken with the very first bath. And if one bathes in this way for a few days, insha-Allah the patient will recover. [The Sharp Sword at the Throat of the Black Magician: 214]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Can Remuneration Be Taken for Performing Ruqyah?
ruqyah_articles.text: Imam Ibn Taymiyyah (rahimahullah) said, "There is no objection to taking compensation for performing ruqyah. There is a clear opinion of Imam Ahmad (rahimahullah) on this matter." [Imam Ibn Taymiyyah, al-Fatawa al-Kubra, 5/408]As proof, we can recall the previous hadith narrated from Abu Sa'eed (RA). The hadith is presented once again in detail: a group of the Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ) were on a journey; they stopped at a settlement of the Arabs. They asked the people of the settlement for hospitality, but the people of the settlement did not entertain the Companions.Meanwhile, a snake bit their tribal chief. Then they said, 'Is there any raqi among you? Because the chief of our settlement is a victim of a snakebite and is afflicted with magic.' From the group it was said, 'Yes, there is. However, you did not entertain us. Therefore, first fix a wage for us, then we will perform ruqyah.' They fixed a flock of sheep. Then a Companion performed ruqyah on the tribal chief by reciting Surah Al-Fatihah. The tribal chief gradually recovered; consequently, a flock of sheep was given to the Companions.Then again, the Companions refused to take the compensation and said, 'Let us tell the Messenger (ﷺ) about the matter first.' They came to the Messenger (ﷺ). The raqi said to the Messenger (ﷺ), 'O Messenger of Allah! Wallahi! I only performed ruqyah on him by reciting Surah Al-Fatihah.' The Messenger (ﷺ) heard everything, smiled, and said, "Who told you that it is ruqyah? Well! Accept them from them, and give me a share from there as well."Imam an-Nawawi (rahimahullah) said, this hadith has made it clear that taking compensation for performing ruqyah with al-Fatihah and the Qur'an is halal without any form of dislike. [an-Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim: 14/188]Even though accepting money for performing ruqyah is permissible, it is the duty of raqi brothers and sisters to keep in mind that the Glorious Qur'an is for everyone and it is not worldly wealth. Therefore, no one should be deprived of the Shar'i treatment, ruqyah, for lack of money. If someone is deprived of ruqyah because of money, this will undoubtedly be an extremely reprehensible act. Referring to the Qur'an as universal, Allah the Almighty says,إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَTranslation: "The Qur'an is but a reminder to the worlds." [Surah Sad 38:87]It is noteworthy that in the aforementioned hadith, the Messenger (ﷺ), by asking for a share of the flock of sheep, made the inquiring Companions understand that there is no doubt regarding this gift being halal.Prerequisites for ruqyah to be effective: Ruqyah is a means of receiving solutions to problems directly from Allah. Therefore, to obtain the results of ruqyah, the raqi must abide by the rulings of Allah the Almighty's commands and prohibitions. Some mandatory rulings for the raqi are mentioned below:1. Abide by the rulings of Shari'ah hijab with all non-mahrams and give priority to all Islamic rulings in daily life;2. If you have taken any kufri amulet (ta'weez) or any such treatment involving shirk or bid'ah, abandon it first and keep your faith in Allah firm;3. Regularly maintain the practice of reciting Surah Al-Baqarah at home;4. Run the family based on mutual consultation. Children may lose mental balance due to family turmoil. Later, all the blame falls upon the jinn!5. Marry off your children at the right time. When illicit relationships break down, in many cases people (especially girls) may lose their balance. When boys and girls get involved in illicit relationships, mercy is lifted; depression is created.6. Whether female or male! Lower your gaze. If female, adhere to the rulings of Shar'i purdah.7. If there are any pictures, statues, or sculptures in the house, remove them first. Otherwise, the angels of mercy will not enter the house and ruqyah will not work.In addition to observing Allah's commands and prohibitions, the raqi must also be socially conscious. For example, in illnesses such as cancer, schizophrenia, or any complex disease, instead of advising only ruqyah, the raqi should advise the patient to go to a doctor. It is often seen that when bitten by a dog, people go to a cleric; again, in the case of a snakebite, many go to an ojha (traditional healer). It is the duty of the raqi to give them proper advice so that, alongside practices from the Qur'an and Sunnah, they immediately seek the help of a doctor.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Is Ruqyah Applicable to Non-Muslims?
ruqyah_articles.text: In answer to this question, it must be said that it is certainly applicable. Because Allah the Almighty has placed shifa in the Qur'an for mankind, just as He has placed shifa in honey and olives. Honey and olives are a cure for everyone, regardless of whether they are Muslim or non-Muslim. Just like honey and olives, there will be no distinction between Muslim and non-Muslim in the case of the Qur'an as well; this is the demand of the broad scope of the Qur'an's (textual) meaning. For Allah has called the Qur'an 'Dhikrul-lil-'Alamin' or a reminder for the entire world.However, the prerequisite for everyone, Muslim or non-Muslim, to benefit from ruqyah is that the reciter of ruqyah must recite with ikhlas (sincerity) and yaqeen (certainty). Since the foundation of ikhlas and yaqeen is iman (faith), the raqi must be a Muslim. We have previously mentioned the hadith of Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri (RA). There we saw that the people of the settlement were not willing to offer hospitality to the traveling Companions; rather, they ignored them.In light of the hadith, Ibn al-Qayyim (rahimahullah) said, 'That settlement of the Arabs either belonged to disbelievers, or their religion was unknown to the Companions; at least this much can be said, they were miserly.' Besides, why did they attach a condition for ruqyah without offering hospitality? The noble Companions, endowed with the virtue of iman, were never miserly. Given the camaraderie that existed among the Companions, had the people of the settlement been Muslim, the question of not offering hospitality would not even arise.Therefore, it can indeed be said that the people of that settlement were perhaps disbelievers. Even so, we saw in the hadith that the chief of the people of the settlement recovered. This proves that ruqyah is applicable to non-Muslims as well.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: The Rationale and Effectiveness of Ruqyah
ruqyah_articles.text: Come! In order to understand the rationale and efficacy of reciting the Qur'an in the treatment of jinn and sihr (magic), let us first read the meanings of Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas:Say, 'I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of that which He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.' (Surah Al-Falaq: 112)"Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the Sovereign of mankind, and the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer (Khannas) from among mankind and jinn, who whispers into the hearts of mankind."- (Surah An-Nas)Several points are noteworthy from the aforementioned two Surahs:1. If the Qur'an were not sufficient for the treatment of jinn, envy, and magic, then Allah's command to seek refuge and the meaning of the two Surahs would have been rendered futile and meaningless! Na'oodhu billah!2. By commanding [us] to seek refuge in these two Surahs, it is as if Allah is showing us the method of Shar'i treatment.3. Allah revealed the entire Glorious Qur'an for action, for personal recitation, and for verbally conveying to others. Even then, in certain places Allah reveals verses saying 'Say'. For example, Allah began Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas with the word 'Say'. That means reciting those verses is an independent act of worship, or the significance of the word 'Say' is that special emphasis is placed on reciting those verses repeatedly. Therefore, to be saved from the evil of jinn, magic, evil eye ('ayn), etc., we must recite the aforementioned two Surahs and protect ourselves by reciting them repeatedly.The regrettable thing is that we ignore the injunction of recitation instructed by Allah; and we only believe in hanging [things]. We hang ta'weez (amulets); we hang sacred threads; and.. and... ta'weez around our neck, ta'weez around the waist, ta'weez on the arm, ta'weez on the door of the house, ta'weez under the pillow, ta'weez on the tree of a shrine... only hanging ta'weez. A child gets scared! Give a ta'weez. A snake has bitten! Give a ta'weez. Cannot have children! Take a ta'weez. Yet open the books of hadith and see! What the practice of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Companions was like.Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri (RA) said, the Messenger (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from jinn and from the evil eye of humans. When Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas were revealed, he adopted these two and abandoned all other recitations. [Jami' at-Tirmidhi, as-Sunan: 2018]Abandoning all other recitations means that he gave greater importance to reciting Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas. Because, besides Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas, there are also several du'a ma'thurah (transmitted supplications) from the Messenger (ﷺ) for seeking refuge from jinn, magic, and the evil eye.The practice of Ruqyah was present among the Companions as well. Let me briefly recount an incident narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari. A group of Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ) came to a settlement in Arabia. But the people of the settlement did not show them hospitality. At that time, a snake bit the chief of this settlement. They said to the visiting Companions, 'Do you have any medicine or anyone who can perform ruqyah?' The Companions said, 'You did not entertain us. Unless a reward is fixed, we will do nothing.' The people of the settlement fixed a flock of sheep for them. Then one Companion performed Ruqyah by reciting Surah Al-Fatihah. By the mercy of Allah, the chief of that settlement was cured.The condition for Ruqyah to be effective is that the recitation of the Qur'anic du'a and Ruqyah must be from the heart; and there must be firm faith in Allah. Why do people go astray even after reciting 'Ihdinas-sirat al-mustaqeem' (O Allah! Guide us to the straight path), the most recited du'a in the world, so many times? Because a du'a that does not come from the heart is merely a hollow supplication. Yunus (AS) was trapped in the belly of the fish. In this distress, there was no outward means of rescue for Yunus (AS). He supplicated to Allah--لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَTransliteration: Laa ilaaha illaa anta subhaanaka innee kuntu minaz-zaalimeen.Translation: 'There is no (true) deity except You. You are pure and exalted. Indeed, I was of the wrongdoers.' [Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87]Allah heard his du'a; He gave him relief. If you think that you will not attain relief by reciting this du'a, then what is the purpose of mentioning this du'a in the Qur'an? Not just Yunus! Allah says,وَكَذَلِكَ نُنجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَTranslation: And thus do We save the believers. [Surah Al-Anbiya 21:88]Remember Ayyub (AS). He was afflicted by the touch of devils and magic and fell ill. He supplicated to Allah. Allah says,وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍTranslation: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, 'Shaytan has touched me with distress and torment.' [Surah Sad 38:41]By means of this du'a, Allah cured Ayyub (AS). Allah Almighty told him to strike the ground with his foot. He struck it. It was seen that cool water gushed forth for bathing and drinking. You can see the incident from verse 41 of Surah Sad. Dear reader! Ruqyah is nothing else; reciting these supplications described in the Qur'an and Hadith is what Ruqyah is called. In Ruqyah, alongside reciting these, we also follow certain treatment methods described in the Qur'an and Hadith.The raqi and the patient must remember that whether Allah will benefit [them] through the recitation of the Qur'an or not is up to Allah. Healing from illness comes to someone through medicine, while someone else dies suffering from that very same illness. Therefore, Ruqyah must be recited with trust; however, one must keep the faith that Allah will certainly reward this recitation in some way or another. Allah says,فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَTranslation: Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost. [Surah Hud: 115]Spread the purity of the Qur'an in a superstitious society. Allah will certainly grant your reward, in sha Allah. In society, as much magic as is done to harm people, even more people fall victim to magic by going to traditional healers (kobiraj) due to superstition. Place your trust in Allah. The decree of Allah is,إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُTranslation: "When He intends a thing and says 'Be', it immediately becomes." [Surah Ya-Sin, 36:82]Do not despair! Do not give up. Do not ignore worldly means either, that is, medical treatment. Look there! Allah aided at Badr by sending five thousand angels. The angels alone were sufficient. Even so, the Muslims had to fight. Because help will indeed come from Allah! But He sees whether the servant is striving according to his capability or not! It was Allah who opened the closed doors of the wife of al-Aziz for Prophet Yusuf. But to receive Allah's help, Prophet Yusuf (AS) did have to run. Allah only wants to see this run from you.Take medical treatment if necessary for physical illnesses.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Incantations That Do Not Qualify as Ruqyah Shar'iyyah
ruqyah_articles.text: Although Ruqyah means incantation, in Islam only that Ruqyah is permitted which is directly taken from the Qur'an and Sunnah. If Ruqyah is performed by reciting something other than the Qur'an and Sunnah, it will never be considered a Shariah-compliant Ruqyah.Such as uttering words of kufr (disbelief) or seeking help from someone other than Allah. However, yes, there is no problem in directly supplicating to Allah in any language for cure and blowing upon the afflicted person. This is permissible. The Messenger (ﷺ) only permitted that Ruqyah in which there is no shirk. The Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'There is no harm in incantations as long as there is no shirk.' [Muslim, as-Sahih: 2200]Apart from this, he prohibited all shirk-based Ruqyah and ta'weez-tiwalah (amulets and charms). The Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'Undoubtedly, incantations, amulets, and tiwalah are shirk.' [Ahmad, al-Musnad: 3615]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Existence
ruqyah_articles.text: The Jinn are beings created with free will, living on earth in a world parallel to mankind. The Arabic word Jinn is from the verb 'Janna' which means to hide or conceal. Thus, they are physically invisible from man as their description suggests. This invisibility is one of the reasons why some people have denied their existence. However, (as will be seen) the effect which the world of the Jinn has upon our world, is enough to refute this modern denial of one of God's creation. The origins of the Jinn can be traced from the Quran and the Sunnah. Allah says:"Indeed We created man from dried clay of black smooth mud. And We created the Jinn before that from the smokeless flame of fire" (Quran 15:26-27)Thus the Jinn were created before man. As for their physical origin, then the Prophet (ﷺ), may the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon him, has confirmed the above verse when he said:"The Angels were created from light and the Jinn from smokeless fire." (Saheeh Muslim)It is this description of the Jinn which tells us so much about them. Because they were created from fire, their nature has generally been fiery and thus their relationship with man has been built upon this. Like humans, they too are required to worship Allah and follow Islam. Their purpose in life is exactly the same as ours, as Allah says: "I did not create the Jinn and mankind except to worship Me." (Quran 51:56)Jinns can thus be Muslims or non-Muslims. However, due to their fiery nature the majority of them are non-Muslims. All these non-Muslim Jinns form a part of the army of the most famous Jinn, Satan. [Unlike Christianity, Islam maintains that Satan (Lucifer) was from the Jinn and not an angel. Angels do not have a free will to disobey]Consequently, these disbelieving Jinns are also called devils. Jinns also become Muslims, as they did in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a group of them were amazed by the recitation of the Quran. Allah orders the Prophet to tell the people of this event:"Say (O' Muhammed): It has been revealed to me that a group of Jinn listened and said; 'Indeed we have heard a marvelous Quran. It guides unto righteousness so we have believed in it, and we will never make partners with our lord'."(Quran 72:1-2)In many aspects of their world, the Jinn are very similar to us. They eat and drink, they marry, have children and they die. The life span however, is far greater than ours. Like us, they will also be subject to a Final Reckoning by Allah the Most High. They will be present with mankind on the Day of Judgment and will either go to Paradise or Hell.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Jinn's fear of humans
ruqyah_articles.text: Ibn Abi Dunya (R) narrated from Mujahid (R): "As I was praying one night, the shape of a young man stood in front of me, so I charged at him to grab him, but he leapt over the wall, then I heard him fall on the other side, and he never came back after that day.Mujahid (R) : They fear you as much as you fear them. So whenever you meet them, do not show your fear - it will encourage them to attack you; attack them instead and they will run away.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Jinn envy humans
ruqyah_articles.text: Ibn al-Qayyim (R) said: "The evil eye has two types: one of Jinn and one of humans. According to an authentic Hadith from Umm Salama (RA), the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a maid in her house, whose face had a black spot; so he (ﷺ) said: "She is under the effect of an evil eye, so treat her with a Ruqya"? [Recorded by al-Bukhari]Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek protection against the Jinn and the evil eye till the Surah al-Falaq and al-Nas were revealed. After they were revealed he stuck to them and discarded everything beside them". [Recorded as Sound by al-Tirmidhi (3/266), and al-Nasa'i (8/271)]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: When do demons spread out?
ruqyah_articles.text: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (RA) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When night falls (or when it is evening), stop your children from going out, for the devils spread out at that time. But when an hour of the night has passed, release them and close the doors and mention Allah's Name, for Satan does not open a closed door.
