One should know that Satan can order people (mainly the pious ones) to do up to seventy acts of goodness, either to attain one act of evil or to let a more rewarding act slip away from them.Only people who are guided by the light of Allah (AJW), by following the Sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ), and being keen of performing the deeds which are most beloved to Allah (SWT) are fully aware of the devil's intentions.If Satan felt unable to manipulate a person during these last stages, he dispatches his army of men and Jinn to harm his reputation, defaming him with all sorts of accusations, such as takfeer (i.e. as someone who easily considered sinful people as kaffars (polytheists), or as a kafir himself) and by misguidance; warning people against him, in order to destroy his rise and his reputation as one of the prominent callers to Allah, and prevent people from benefiting from his knowledge.This is clear in our society; in fact, whenever a person clings to his/her religion, and adheres to the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ), by following his Sunnah, he/she finds himself at the centre of mockery and opposition from his/her relatives, friends, enemies, etc. So his/her only refuge is with Allah (SWT).This is the situation of people who are attached to Islam inwardly and outwardly; they are strangers who received glad tidings from the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "Islam came as something strange, and it would revert to its old position of being strange; so good tidings to the strangers." [Recorded by Muslim]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: As well as adhering to the Ruqyah program, what else should the patient do?
ruqyah_articles.text: The patient should strengthen himself, arm himself with patience and not give in to despair. The sick person should realize that patience in bearing calamities is the essential outcome of faith and belief in the divine will and decree. Belief in the divine will and decree is one of the six pillars of faith.He should also understand that whatever calamity has befallen him has happened with Allah's knowledge and was decreed by Him fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Allah says: أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّـهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۗ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ فِي كِتَابٍ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّـهِ يَسِيرٌ ﴿٧٠﴾ Translation: "Know you not that Allah knows all that is in heaven and on the earth? Verily, it is (all) in the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfooz). Verily, that is easy for Allah." (Al-Hajj 22:70) مَا أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّبْرَأَهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّـهِ يَسِيرٌ ﴿٢٢﴾ Translation: "No calamity befalls on the earth or in yourselves but it is inscribed in the Book of Decrees (Al-Lawh AlMahfooz) before We bring it into existence. Verily, that is easy for Allah. In order that you may not grieve at the things over that you fail to get, nor rejoice over that which has been given to you." (Al-Hadeed 57:22-23) Once a person understands that whatever befalls him happens with the knowledge of Allah and by His decree, then he must have faith, be patient, accept it and submit to the will of Allah. Once a person has faith and acceptance, then Allah will guide his heart and enable him to be content, to seek reward, to be patient and to give thanks. Whoever is blessed with guidance will find peace of mind, as Allah says: مَا أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّـهِ ۗ وَمَن يُؤْمِن بِاللَّـهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ ۚ وَاللَّـهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ ﴿١١﴾ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّـهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ ۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَىٰ رَسُولِنَا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ ﴿١٢﴾ Translation: "No calamity befalls, but by the Leave li.e. Decision and Qadar (Divine Preordainments)] of Allah, and whosoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart (to the true Faith with certainty, i.e. what has befallen him was already written for him by Allah from the Qadar (Divine Preordainments)). And Allah is the All-Knower of everything, Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger (Muhammad); but if you turn away, then the duty of Our Messenger is only to convey (the Message) clearly." (Al-Taghaabun 64:11-12) One thing that will help a person to achieve that is belief in the will and decree of Allah, and the belief that man has no control over his affairs in this life, rather he does not have control over even the most personal of matters, or his provision, or his lifespan, or whether he is destined to be doomed or blessed. All of that is decreed for him. Anyone who is faced with calamity should understand that a good outcome comes with patience, and that relief will follow distress, and that with hardship comes ease. It was narrated that Ibn 'Abbaas ra. said: I was behind the Prophet (ﷺ) one day and he said to me:"O young man, I will teach you some words (of advice). Be mindful of Allah, and Allah will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you. If you ask, ask of Allah; if you seek help, seek help of Allah. Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with anything, it would benefit you only with something that Allah has already decreed for you, and if they were to gather together to harm you with anything, they would harm you only with something that Allah has already decreed for you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."[Saheeh Hadeeth. See Saheeh Al-Jaami' by Shaykh Al-Albaani (may Allah have mercy on him), no. 7957; Saheeh Muslim; AlTirmidhi] According to some reports: "Remember Allah at times of ease and He will remember you at times of hardship. Understand that whatever misses you would never have befallen you, and whatever befalls you would never have missed you. Understand that a good outcome comes with patience, that relief follows distress and that with hardship comes ease." The person who has been smitten with a calamity must remember the promise of Allah, that a great reward and high status will come to the one who is patient, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said:"A man would have a high status before Allah which he cannot attain by means of good deeds; Allah will continue to test him with things that he dislikes until He causes him to reach that status."[A Hasan Hadeeth. See Saheeh Al-Jaami' by Al-Albaani, no. 1625]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: As well as adhering to the Ruqyah program, what else should the patient do?
ruqyah_articles.text: The patient should be certain that the Healer is Allah alone, and that the Ruqyah comes under the heading of following the means prescribed in Sharee'ah for seeking healing. What counts in Ruqyah is that what is recited --namely the words of Allah, which are as Allah says: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۙ وَلَا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا ﴿٨٢﴾ Translation: "And We send down of the Qur'aan that which is a healing and a mercy to those who believe." (Al-Isra' 17:82) The basic principle is that what counts in Ruqyah is what is recited, not the one who recites it, so we should not let out hearts become attached to individuals.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: As well as adhering to the Ruqyah program, what else should the patient do?
ruqyah_articles.text: The sick person should turn to Allah and make Du'aa'. This is one of the most effective means of warding off that which is disliked, and is one of the most efficacious of remedies. If all the necessary conditions are met, Du'aa' is the enemy of calamity; it wards it off and remedies it, prevents it befalling, and relieves it if it has happened. Du'aa' is the weapon of the believer.Persisting in making Du'aa' is a powerful weapon which will prevent sickness from occurring, and ward it off if it does occur. The Muslim should offer Du'aa' with presence of mind, not with a wandering mind such that the Du'aa' comes out weakly because it comes from a weak heart that is like a slack bow from which arrows come weakly.Thawbaan (RA) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nothing repels the divine decree except Du'aa'; nothing increases one's lifespan except righteousness; and a man may be deprived of provision because of a sin that he committed."[Da'eef Al-Jaami' by Al-Albaani, 1453]Similarly one should not be too hasty in seeking a response to Du'aa', and give up Du'aa' saying, I made Du'aa' but I received no response. In Saheeh AlBukhaari it is narrated from Abu Hurayrah (RA) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Any one of you will receive a response (to his Du'aa') so long as he is not hasty and says, 'I made Du'aa' but I received no response."According to Saheeh Muslim, it was said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what does being hasty mean?" He said: "When one says, 'I made Du'aa' and I made Du'aa' and I received no response, and he feels frustrated and stops making Du'aa'.The one who raises his hands to Allah in supplication should also be keen to seek what is Halaal in his food, drink and clothing. Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated that Abu Hurayrah ra. said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, Allah is Good and only accepts that which is good. Allah enjoins upon the believers that which He enjoined upon the Messengers, as He said: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ Translation: "O you who believe (in the Oneness of Allah - Islamic Monotheism)! Eat of the lawful things that we have provided you with." (Al-Baqarah 2:172)Then he mentioned a man who has undertaken a lengthy journey, he is disheveled and dusty, and he stretches his hands towards the heavens saying, "O Lord, O Lord," but his food is Haraam, his clothing is Haraam, he has been nourished with Haraam so how can he receive any response?He should also seek out the six times when Du'aa's are answered, which are:1. The last third of the night 2. When the Adhaan is given 3. Between the Adhaan and Iqaamah. 4. Following the obligatory prayers 5. When the Imam ascends the Minbar on Friday, and until the prayers of that day are over6. The last hour after 'Asr prayer on Friday.Finally, Du'aa should come from a heart that is humble, broken before Allah, submitting to Him and beseeching with humility, whilst facing towards the Qiblah with the hands raised, and choosing appropriate words. Whoever is guided to make Du'aa' will receive a response. He should also be in a state of purity. He should start by praising and glorifying Allah, then send blessings and salaams upon the Messenger of Allah then he should address Allah by His most beautiful names and sublime attributes. Then he should humbly persist in asking of Allah, weeping before Him, calling upon Him in hope and fear, and thinking positively of Allah, and he should do that a great deal. It is also recommended to give in charity before making Du'aa', giving good and Halaal things, from the dearest of one's wealth.If the Du'aa' is offered in this manner, then it can hardly be refused, especially if one uses the Du'aa's that the Prophet (ﷺ) said are likely to bring a response, which include the greatest Name of Allah.I also say to everyone who is faced with calamity, everyone who is sick, and indeed every Muslim: who among us does not possess this powerful weapon, namely Du'aa'? So make Du'aa', and use this powerful weapon. You have a fine example to follow in the noblest of creation, the beloved of Allah, our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) He made Du'aa', beseeching Allah, and he used to raise his hands towards heaven in supplication until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen, and until his cloak fell from his shoulders, even though he was infallible and his previous and future sins had been forgiven.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: As well as adhering to the Ruqyah program, what else should the patient do?
ruqyah_articles.text: The sick person should pray a great deal for forgiveness, and repent, and say: إِنَّا للّٰهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَا جِعُونَ. Transliteration: "Inna Lilaahi wa inna ilayhi Raaji'oon.Translation: Truly, to Allah we belong and truly, to Him we shall return."and, لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ. Transliteration: "Laa hawla wa laa quwwata illa Billaah.Translation: There is no power and no strength except with Allah" and, حَسْبُنَا اللّٰه وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ. Transliteration: "Hasbunaa Allah wa ni'ma Al-wakeel.Translation: Allah (Alone) is Sufficient for us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs.". The sick person must frequently recite his daily Wird and recite Qur'aan, and read Soorah Al Baqarah, at least once every three days.. The sick person must regularly recite the Adhkaar for morning and evening, which we will discuss under a separate heading in the chapter on prayers for protection.. He should do a lot of Nawafil acts of worship, namely fasting and praying.. He should try to keep his Wudoo' as much as possible.. He should not start any action except in the name of Allah, especially eating and drinking.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ten ways of avoiding the harm of the Jinn and protecting oneself against the devils
ruqyah_articles.text: 1. Seeking refuge with Allah from the traps of the devils.2. Reciting Al-Falaq and An-Naas, because it was narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) vetem used to seek refuge with Allah from the jinn and the evil eye of people, until these two Soorahs were revealed.3. Reciting Aayat Al-kursi.4. Reciting Soorah Al-Baqarah.5. Reciting the last two verses of Soorah Al-Baqarah.6. Reciting the first part of Soorah Ghaafir.7. Frequently repeating the words: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللّٰهُ،وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ Transliteration: "Laa ilaaha ill-Allah wahdahu laa shareeka lahu, lahu'l-mulk wa lahu'l-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer.Translation: There is no Allah but Allah alone, with no partner or associate; His is the Dominion, to Him be all praise, and He has power over all things." 8. Frequently remembering Allah (Dhikr), which includes regularly reciting the Adhkaar which are to be said in various situations and when doing certain things, as mentioned in Chapter 5 of this book. 9. Wudoo' and prayer.10. Refraining from unnecessary looking, speaking,eating and mixing with people, because going to extremes in these four matters weakens one's spirituality and makes it easy for the evil ones among mankind and the jinn to gain power over you.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: The jinn are a creation of Allah. Just as He created angels and humans, He also created the jinn. They possess intellect, reason, and perception. They have the ability to distinguish between good and evil. Among them are good jinn and bad jinn. Mentioning the statement of the jinn in the Qur'an, it is stated:وَّ اَنَّا مِنَّا الصّٰلِحُوۡنَ وَ مِنَّا دُوۡنَ ذٰلِکَ ؕ کُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدًا ﴿ۙ۱۱﴾Translation: 'And among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so; we were of divided ways.' (Surah Al-Jinn: 11)This group has been named jinn because the word jinn means hidden. From the Arabic word jinn, ijtinan means istitar or being concealed. As Allah has said in the Qur'an:فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَیۡہِ الَّیۡلُTranslation: So when the night covered him... (Surah Al-An'am: 76)Here, janna means to cover, to be enveloped, or to be concealed. Because they remain hidden from human sight, they have been named jinn. As Allah, the Lord of the worlds, says:اِنَّہٗ یَرٰىکُمۡ ہُوَ وَ قَبِیۡلُہٗ مِنۡ حَیۡثُ لَا تَرَوۡنَہُمۡTranslation: Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. (Surah Al-A'raf: 27)The jinn were created from fire. The Almighty Creator Allah says:وَ الۡجَآنَّ خَلَقۡنٰہُ مِنۡ قَبۡلُ مِنۡ نَّارِ السَّمُوۡمِ ﴿۲۷﴾Translation: And the jinn We created before from scorching fire. (Surah Al-Hijr: 27)From this verse, we also learn that Allah, the Lord of the worlds, created the jinn before creating mankind. It has been stated:وَ لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا الۡاِنۡسَانَ مِنۡ صَلۡصَالٍ مِّنۡ حَمَاٍ مَّسۡنُوۡنٍ ﴿ۚ۲۶﴾ وَ الۡجَآنَّ خَلَقۡنٰہُ مِنۡ قَبۡلُ مِنۡ نَّارِ السَّمُوۡمِ ﴿۲۷﴾Translation: And We did certainly create man out of dried clay of altered black mud. And the jinn We created before from scorching fire. (Surah Al-Hijr: 26-27)The purpose for which Allah created mankind is the very purpose for which He created the jinn. He says:وَ مَا خَلَقۡتُ الۡجِنَّ وَ الۡاِنۡسَ اِلَّا لِیَعۡبُدُوۡنِ ﴿۵۶﴾Translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. (Surah Adh-Dhariyat: 56)He also sent prophets and messengers to the jinn. He says:یٰمَعۡشَرَ الۡجِنِّ وَ الۡاِنۡسِ اَلَمۡ یَاۡتِکُمۡ رُسُلٌ مِّنۡکُمۡ یَقُصُّوۡنَ عَلَیۡکُمۡ اٰیٰتِیۡ وَ یُنۡذِرُوۡنَکُمۡ لِقَآءَ یَوۡمِکُمۡ ہٰذَا ؕ قَالُوۡا شَہِدۡنَا عَلٰۤی اَنۡفُسِنَا وَ غَرَّتۡہُمُ الۡحَیٰوۃُ الدُّنۡیَا وَ شَہِدُوۡا عَلٰۤی اَنۡفُسِہِمۡ اَنَّہُمۡ کَانُوۡا کٰفِرِیۡنَ ﴿۱۳۰﴾Translation: 'O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'We bear witness against ourselves'; and the worldly life deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers. (Surah Al-An'am: 130)This verse clearly proves that just as humans will be judged on the Day of Judgment, the jinn will likewise have to face judgment and accountability.It has come in the hadith that they can take on various forms. Likewise, it is mentioned in Surah An-Naml of the Qur'an that they can move swiftly from one place to another.Those who believe in the heavenly scriptures--Jews, Christians, and Muslims--all believe in the existence of the jinn. None of them deny the existence of the jinn. Polytheists, some philosophers, and materialist researchers do not deny the existence of the jinn. A group of philosophers say that angels and jinn are used in a metaphorical sense. Good character is meant by the word angel, and bad character by the word jinn or Shaytan. However, this statement of theirs is completely contrary to the Qur'an and Sunnah.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding this, the jinn are of three types--1. Those who fly in the air.2. Some are snakes and dogs.3. Those who come to humans and leave.(Reference: at-Tabarani. The renowned hadith scholar Shaykh al-Albani classified the hadith as sahih. See: Sahih al-Jami' as-Saghir, Hadith no. 3114, narrated from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani (RA).) (Mu'jam Alfadh al-Aqidah)The jinn can take on the form of various animals. But a group of them always moves about in human society in the form of snakes and dogs. This is their permanent form.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: A Muslim must acknowledge the existence of the jinn. If he denies the existence of the jinn, he will not remain a believer. Acknowledging the existence of the jinn is included in Iman bil-Ghayb (belief in the unseen). Allah, Lord of the worlds, has discussed the jinn nearly fifty times in the Qur'an.The creation of the jinn, the purpose of their creation, their acceptance of Islam, their creation before mankind, Iblees being from among the jinn, addressing the jinn and mankind together in Surah Ar-Rahman, the jinn working during the time of Prophet Sulaiman (AS), the mention of builders and divers being among them, their facing judgment, punishment, and reward on the Day of Resurrection--Allah, Lord of the worlds, has mentioned many such details in the Qur'an. Speaking about them, He revealed a complete surah named Surah Al-Jinn.Therefore, no Muslim can commit an act like denying the Word of Allah by denying the existence of the jinn. Likewise, one cannot even think of using the jinn in a metaphorical sense. This is the aqeedah of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah. The deviant and extinct Mu'tazilah and Jahmiyyah sects do not acknowledge the existence of the jinn.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: The answer to this is: indeed, jinn can afflict humans. They can drive them mad through touch. They can possess humans. They can control them. They can disrupt the normal activities of their lives.This must be believed. However, if anyone disbelieves in this matter, they cannot be called a kafir (disbeliever). It will be said that they have made a mistake.Some proofs that jinn afflict humans:Allah, Lord of the worlds, says:اَلَّذِیۡنَ یَاۡکُلُوۡنَ الرِّبٰوا لَا یَقُوۡمُوۡنَ اِلَّا کَمَا یَقُوۡمُ الَّذِیۡ یَتَخَبَّطُہُ الشَّیۡطٰنُ مِنَ الۡمَسِّTranslation: Those who consume interest will stand like one whom Satan by his touch drives to madness. (Surah Al-Baqarah: 275)The matters that are clearly understood from this verse: One, an idea about the nature of the punishment for those who consume interest. Two, Satan or jinn can drive humans like mad through touch. Three, the touch of Satan or jinn upon humans is a reality. There is no way to deny this. Four, through this touch of jinn-Satan, just as humans are harmed spiritually, they also become abnormal physically. Allah Ta'ala says:وَ مَنۡ یَّعۡشُ عَنۡ ذِکۡرِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ نُقَیِّضۡ لَہٗ شَیۡطٰنًا فَہُوَ لَہٗ قَرِیۡنٌ ﴿۳۶﴾Translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion. (Surah Az-Zukhruf: 36)What is made clear by this verse is: abstaining from the dhikr of Allah Ta'ala, the Most Merciful and Compassionate, is a reason for being harmed by the touch of jinn and Satan.Allah Ta'ala says:وَاذۡکُرۡ عَبۡدَنَاۤ اَیُّوۡبَ ۘ اِذۡ نَادٰی رَبَّہٗۤ اَنِّیۡ مَسَّنِیَ الشَّیۡطٰنُ بِنُصۡبٍ وَّ عَذَابٍ ﴿ؕ۴۱﴾Translation: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment.' (Surah Sad: 41)From this verse, we clearly understood:1. Satan touched Prophet Ayyub (AS) and increased his physical illness and suffering.2. He prayed to Allah Ta'ala alone to be saved from the touch of Satan.Allah Ta'ala says:اِنَّ الَّذِیۡنَ اتَّقَوۡا اِذَا مَسَّہُمۡ طٰٓئِفٌ مِّنَ الشَّیۡطٰنِ تَذَکَّرُوۡا فَاِذَا ہُمۡ مُّبۡصِرُوۡنَ ﴿۲۰۱﴾ۚTranslation: Indeed, those who have adopted taqwa -- when an evil whisper from Satan touches them, they remember Allah, and at once their eyes are opened. (Surah Al-A'raf: 201)What is understood from this verse is: One, those who are muttaqeen (God-fearing) can also be touched by jinn or Satan. Even being muttaqeen, they can fall victim to the affliction of jinn or Satan. Two, when Satan or jinn touches those who are muttaqeen, they remember Allah alone. They do not turn to anything else.Three. When the muttaqeen are touched by jinn or Satan and remember Allah, their true vision is opened. Allah Ta'ala says:وَ اِمَّا یَنۡزَغَنَّکَ مِنَ الشَّیۡطٰنِ نَزۡغٌ فَاسۡتَعِذۡ بِاللّٰہِ ؕ اِنَّہٗ سَمِیۡعٌ عَلِیۡمٌ ﴿۲۰۰﴾Translation: And if an evil suggestion from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. (Surah Al-A'raf: 200)In this verse, it is clearly proven:1. Jinn-Satan can afflict even the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).2. When jinn afflict or when the evil whispers of Satan are felt, it is commanded to seek refuge in Allah.Three. Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are extremely valuable words for seeking refuge from the affliction of jinn and Satan. This is proven by the tafseer of this verse.It has come in the hadith:Narrated from Aisha (RA), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed, Satan is capable of circulating through the veins and arteries of human blood. (Narrated by: Bukhari and Muslim) It has also come in the hadith that one day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:Last night, a powerful jinn wanted to attack me. His intention was to ruin my prayer. Allah gave me power over him. (Narrated by: Bukhari, Book of Salah)Imam Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (rahimahullah) said in the explanation of this hadith that in the narration of an-Nasa'i from Aisha (RA), it has further come that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I grabbed him, threw him down, and throttled him. I even felt the moisture of his tongue on my hand.What we learned from this hadith:1. The jinn wanted to afflict even the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).2. The jinn came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ruin his prayer.3. The Bengali meaning of the word Ifrit is ghost. Those among the jinn who are wicked and rowdy in nature are called Ifrit.4. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not feel any fear upon seeing the jinn. He fought with him and defeated him.5. Jinn have a body or structure, although it is generally not visible to us.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: Jinn is an Arabic word. The word jinn is also used in Bengali. But ghost is a Bengali word. Its Arabic is Ifrit, plural Afarit. In the Qur'an, in verse 39 of Surah An-Naml, the word Ifrit has appeared like this:قَالَ عِفۡرِیۡتٌ مِّنَ الۡجِنِّ اَنَا اٰتِیۡکَ بِہٖ قَبۡلَ اَنۡ تَقُوۡمَ مِنۡ مَّقَامِکَ ۚ وَ اِنِّیۡ عَلَیۡہِ لَقَوِیٌّ اَمِیۡنٌ ﴿۳۹﴾Translation: A powerful jinn said, 'I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am strong and trustworthy regarding this.' (Surah An-Naml: 39)In this verse, the words 'Ifritum minal-jinn', that is, 'an Ifrit or ghost from among the jinn...', have appeared. Likewise, in the hadith mentioned above, the words 'Ifritum minal-jinn' have also appeared. Commentators of the Qur'an have said that those among the jinn who are disobedient, unruly, rowdy, wicked in nature, and powerful are called Ifrit. (Al-Mufradat fi Gharib al-Qur'an)The meaning of the word Ifrit in Bengali is ghost.Therefore, it is seen that an Ifrit or ghost is nothing other than a jinn. All ghosts are jinn, but not all jinn are ghosts.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: Often we fall into this problem. We cannot determine whether the illness is mental, or madness, or whether the illness has arisen from the affliction of jinn. That is why we often call a mental patient a jinn-possessed patient. Likewise, we try to pass off a jinn-possessed patient as a mental patient. Especially doctors and psychiatrists do not want to acknowledge the affliction of jinn in any way. They identify all such patients as mental patients. Madness is called Junoon in Arabic. And a mad person is called Majnoon. But in Arabic, both these words, Junoon and Majnoon, are derived from the word Jinn. As it has come in the Qur'an:إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلُۢ بِهِۦ جِنَّةࣱ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ حِینࣲTranslation: "He is only a man in whom is madness, so wait concerning him for a time." [Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:25]The people of the nation of Nuh (AS) said this about him. In this verse, the meaning of the word Jinnatun is madness. Therefore, seeing someone behave abnormally like madness can be due to the affliction of jinn, or it can also be due to mental illness. However, experts in this field have determined some points in the light of experience, through which a distinction can be made between a mental patient and a jinn-possessed patient. These are:1. A jinn-possessed patient becomes unconscious for a while. A mental patient does not fall unconscious.2. Sometimes foam comes out of the mouth of a jinn-possessed patient. The teeth lock together. Foam does not come out of the mouth of a mental patient.3. A jinn-possessed patient often sees snakes, dogs, scorpions, monkeys, jackals, rats, etc., in dreams. Sometimes they dream that they are falling from a very high place.4. A jinn-possessed patient always has a fearful disposition. They always feel afraid. A mental patient does not have such fear.5. A jinn-possessed patient does not like performing salah, reciting the Qur'an, dhikr of Allah, etc. Rather, these increase their restlessness.6. A jinn-possessed patient sometimes speaks in a different language and in a different tone.7. A jinn-possessed patient remains normal most of the time. Occasionally, they behave abnormally.8. Many astonishing things are often manifested by a jinn-possessed patient. For example, they go far away in a short time, climb up trees and sit on thin branches, etc.9. A jinn-possessed patient does not like their husband, household, wife, and children.10. When a jinn overpowers a jinn-possessed patient, if a picture of them is taken with a camera, the picture becomes hazy like smoke. It has been seen that pictures of everyone around came out clearly, but the patient's picture is hazy. This is the personal experience of some people. It must be remembered that experience may not always give the same result.However, a major problem arises when the patient pretends to be possessed by a jinn, but jinn has not afflicted them, nor are they a mental patient. They are pretending to be possessed by a jinn to fulfill an objective of their own. In this situation, what the guardians should do is give them assurance of fulfilling their demand. Then their jinn will leave. Later, if their demand is reasonable, it will be fulfilled, and if it is unreasonable, it will not be fulfilled. After this, if they pretend to be possessed by a jinn again, there is no need to believe them as a jinn-possessed patient anymore. Often, if threatened with physical punishment, this kind of fake jinn goes away.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: There are some matters due to the presence of which jinn afflict humans-1. Love. If a male jinn falls in love with a woman, or if a female jinn falls in love with a man, then the jinn afflicts that beloved person.2. If a human oppresses, mistreats, or harms a jinn, then the oppressed jinn attacks that person. For example, if someone strikes a jinn, throws hot water on it, or destroys its food, the jinn attacks that person.3. Jinn attack humans without reason to oppress and torment them. However, this can happen due to five reasons:(a) Excessive anger(b) Excessive fear(c) Loss of sexual desire(d) Extreme heedlessness.(e) Remaining dirty and impure.If these traits are present in someone, jinn get the opportunity to afflict and torment them.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: What Islam Says About Jinn Possession
ruqyah_articles.text: The manner of jinn overpowering humans can be of four types--1. The jinn exerts influence over the human's entire body for some time.2. Partially, it exerts influence over one or more parts of the body for some time. Such as in the hand, or foot, or mouth.3. The jinn can permanently overpower the human body. Its duration can be very long. Fourth, it exerts influence over the human mind for some time. When the person begins seeking refuge in Allah, it leaves.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Symptoms of Being Possessed by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Certainly, there are some signs and symptoms of the evil eye ('ayn), sihr (magic), and jinn possession that appear in the patient. These are similar to one another, making it very difficult to distinguish between them. It is not a condition that all of these be found together in the patient. Rather, sometimes some signs appear. And sometimes they occur due to physical or psychological illnesses, which have no connection to the evil eye, sihr, or jinn possession. It is essential to be cautious regarding these matters. The symptoms and signs can be divided into two parts, such as:Signs that are observed in the patient before performing ruqyah:1. Suddenly, a loved thing turning into hatred or a hated thing turning into love.2. Suffering from various types and frequent illnesses without any clear medical cause.3. Feeling constriction in the heart, especially after 'Asr and Maghrib salah.4. Dislike of work, reluctance toward society and studies, and preferring to be alone.5. Imagining having done various things when in reality one has not done them.6. The face turning pale or yellow, or bluish or brownish marks appearing on the body without any known cause.7. Recurrent headaches or sudden fever.8. Constant quarrels and disputes between husband and wife, and hatred continually increasing between the two; or family members severing relations over trivial and minor matters.9. Having the impression of seeing various fanciful dreams while awake.10. Laziness and inactivity, constantly feeling tired, and having no appetite for food and drink.11. Repeatedly feeling a lack of balance while walking.12. Repeatedly hearing a whooshing sound in both ears or in one ear.13. Women experiencing lower abdominal pain or bleeding, especially during menstruation; or frequent istihadah, that is, discharge-leukorrhea gynecological issues.14. Becoming intensely angry over small matters.15. Constant desire to sleep, and feeling distress after waking from deep sleep.16. Hearing as if someone is calling one's name, but seeing no one.17. Constantly feeling ongoing pain in the lower back, middle of the back, or between both shoulders.18. Skin allergy that itches, abdominal bloating, and sometimes rashes appearing on the body.19. Frequent severe dysentery, or excessive gas in the stomach, acidity or burning sensation, or chronic constipation.20. Loss of vision and clearly seeing things distorted.21. Constant anxiety, insomnia, restlessness, panic, and extreme fear.22. Strong and severe waswasa (doubts and misgivings) arising in the mind.23. The mind constantly being restless and excessive forgetfulness.24. Hindrance from the dhikr of Allah and developing an aversion to performing acts of worship.25. Abnormal sweat odor or a strange foul smell, or an odor that the patient smells but no one nearby does; in addition to excessive sweating or frequent urination.26. Weakening of sexual potency and showing reluctance towards intercourse on the part of the husband or wife; seeing distressing creatures, such as: black snakes or black dogs or black cats; besides seeing other things such as: camels or graveyards or garbage dumping grounds, or falling from above, or drowning in deep water, etc.28. Frequently talking in sleep, loudly grinding teeth, sighing, and crying suddenly.29. Repeatedly feeling an immense heaviness upon the chest in sleep.30. Frequently walking around in sleep, or recurrent insomnia, or standing up from sleep in a panicked state.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Symptoms of Being Possessed by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: 1. Falling to the ground or having convulsions.2. Feeling constriction in the chest.3. Rapid movement of the eyelashes.4. Screaming intensely.5. Stomach pain and rumbling sounds or abdominal bloating.6. Change in voice or strange sounds coming out.7. Swelling of a vein in the neck.8. Drowsiness or falling asleep.9. Laughing or crying without any reason.10. Dizziness or bodily malaise, or vomiting and things of abnormal shape and color coming out with the vomit.11. Having a severe headache.12. Feeling heaviness on a side of the body, or numbness, or feeling a pricking sensation, or extreme heat or extreme cold.13. Feeling as if a part from the side of the body is falling off.14. Experiencing various types of temporary pain in the body.15. Trembling in certain parts of the body.16. Excessive phlegm coming out.17. Clearly seeing things distorted or seeing mustard flowers.18. Speaking without one's own awareness.19. Excessive sweating, especially on the back.20. Tears coming from the eyes or water running from the nose without any cold, etc.21. Repeated yawning or sighing.22. Itching on the body, rashes, or redness.23. Feeling severe inability during self-ruqyah and reluctance to complete it.24. Trembling starting throughout the entire body.25. Fainting and increased breathing.26. The face turning dark, and the face brightening when the patient vomits.27. A severe foul odor coming out through the mouth from the stomach.28. Sudden increase in heartbeat and continuing to increase.29. Closing both eyes or staring with wide eyes.30. Feeling a bitter taste in the mouth while drinking water blown upon with certain verses of the Qur'an.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: Because Allah Ta'ala has said:وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَانًا فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌTranslation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. (Surah Az-Zukhruf: 36)It has come in the hadith -The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when any of you goes to sleep, Shaytan sits near his head and ties three knots. At the time of tying each knot, he says one thing: A long night lies before you, so sleep. When he wakes from sleep and remembers Allah, one knot is untied. Then when he performs wudu, another knot is untied. After that, when he prays salah, the last knot is untied. As a result, he spends the day energetic and in good spirits. And if he does not do so, then he spends the day in a bad mood and laziness. (Narrated by: al-Bukhari and Muslim)From this hadith it is proven:1. By properly performing wudu and praying salah, one can remain free from the onslaught of Shaytan.2. Being in a bad mood and laziness are the result of Shaytan's whisperings.3. By regularly performing salah, the body and mind remain cheerful. Activity and vigor increase. Laziness is dispelled.4. Immediately upon waking from sleep, before performing wudu or ghusl, one should remember Allah. There is a specific du'a for waking up from sleep. Reciting it is Sunnah. Through this, the evil influence of Shaytan is dispelled.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: It has come in the hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:Whoever says when leaving the house,بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِTransliteration: Bismillaahi, tawakkaltu 'alallaahi, laa hawla wa laa quwwata illaa billaah.Translation: In the name of Allah, relying upon Allah I set out. And there is no way to be saved from sin except by His ability, and no good deed can be done except by His strength.Then it is said to him, this is sufficient for you, you have been protected, and you have been guided. And Shaytan moves away from him. (Narrated by: Sunan Abi Dawud and Jami' at-Tirmidhi)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: It has come in the hadith -When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the toilet, he used to say -بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِTransliteration: Bismillaah, Allaahumma, innee a'oodhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khabaa'ithTranslation: In the name of Allah. O Allah! I seek refuge in You from male and female devils. (Narrated by: al-Bukhari and Muslim)In another narration it has come, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Jinn and devils reside in these toilet places. Therefore, when any of you comes here, he should say, Allaahumma, innee a'oodhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khabaa'ith. (Narrated by: Ibn Hibban)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَTransliteration: A'oodhu bikalimaatillaahit-taammaati, min sharri maa khalaqTranslation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created. (Narrated by: Muslim, Jami' at-Tirmidhi, Musnad Ahmad)In another narration it has come,A person came to the Noble Prophet (ﷺ) and said, last night a scorpion stung me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, did I not tell you that when evening comes you should say,أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَTransliteration: A'oodhu bikalimaatillaahit-taammaati, min sharri maa khalaqthen nothing could have harmed you. (Narrated by: Muslim, Hadith no. 2709)In yet another narration it has come - a jinn wanted to possess the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There was another jinn with him. Jibreel came and said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), you say these words, then they will not be able to do anything to you. (Narrated by: Ibn Abi Hatim)Likewise, when someone goes to any place and recites this du'a, then nothing will be able to harm him.The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, whoever alights at a place and then says:أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَTransliteration: A'oodhu bikalimaatillaahit-taammaati, min sharri maa khalaqTranslation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.then nothing will be able to harm him, as long as he stays there. (Narrated by: Muslim, from Khawlah bint Hakim)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: It has come in the hadith -قلت: يا رسول اللَّه شكا حاجة شديدة وعيالا ، فرحمته فخليت سبيله ، قال: ( أما إنه كذبك ، وسيعود ) . فرصدته الثالثة ، فجاء يحثو من الطعام ، فأخذته فقلت: لأرفعنك إلى رسول اللَّه ، وهذا آخر ثلاث مرات تزعم لا تعود ، ثم تعود ، قال: دعني أعلمك كلمات ينفعك اللَّه بها ، قلت ماNarrated from Abu Hurairah (RA) (RA), he said, in a month of Ramadan, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me the responsibility of guarding the wealth of zakah. I saw a visitor come and reach his hands into the food to take some. I caught him. And I said, by Allah! I will definitely take you to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said, I am a very poor man. I have a family. My need is dire. Abu Hurairah (RA) said, I let him go. In the morning, when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said, what happened, Abu Hurairah (RA)! What is the news of your prisoner from last night? I said, O Messenger of Allah! He told me of his extreme need. I took pity on him and let him go. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, indeed he lied to you. You will see, he will come again.From these words, I understood that he would certainly come again. Because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said he would come again. I waited in anticipation. The next night he came again and began searching with his hands among the food. I caught him. And I said, by Allah, I will definitely take you to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said, let me go. I am very helpless. I have a family. I will not come again. This time too, I took pity on him and let him go. In the morning, when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said, what happened, Abu Hurairah (RA)! What did your prisoner do last night? I said, O Messenger of Allah! He told me of his severe need. He has a family. I took pity on him and let him go. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, indeed he lied to you. Look, he will come again.On the third day I waited in anticipation, he came again, put his hands into the food, and began searching. I caught him. And I said, by Allah, I will definitely take you to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). You have come for the last of three times. You said you would not come. Yet you have come again. He said, let me go. I will teach you some words that will be of great benefit to you. I said, what are those words? He said, when you go to sleep, recite Ayatul Kursi. Then a protector from Allah will guard you and Shaytan will not be able to come near you until morning. I let him go.In the morning, when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said, what happened, Abu Hurairah (RA)! What did your prisoner do last night? I said, Ya Rasulullah! He taught me some beneficial words, so I let him go. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked, what did he teach you? I said, he said, when you go to sleep, recite Ayatul Kursi. Then a protector from Allah will guard you and Shaytan will not be able to come near you until morning.The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, he told you the truth although he is a liar. O Abu Hurairah (RA)! Do you know who it was you have been speaking to for the past three nights?Abu Hurairah (RA) said, no, I do not know. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, that was Shaytan. (Narrated by: al-Bukhari)What we learn from this hadith is:1. It is a duty to appoint a trustworthy, responsible person to guard and protect public wealth. Abu Hurairah (RA) (RA) was a trustworthy, reliable Sahabi.2. Abu Hurairah (RA) (RA) showed devotion and sincerity in fulfilling his responsibility. He guarded the wealth of zakah without sleeping even at night.3. This is a miracle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that without being present at the scene, he understood the matter of Shaytan's arrival merely upon hearing the narration from Abu Hurairah (RA).4. The compassion of the Sahabah towards the poor and helpless who bear the burdens of their families, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recognized this compassion. He did not say to Abu Hurairah (RA) (RA), why did you let him go? Why did you show mercy?5. How great the value of knowledge was to the Sahabah that when the criminal Shaytan wanted to teach him something, he learned it and, in appreciation of it, even let him go.6. If an evil or dishonest person or a jinn shaytan teaches something good, there is no harm in learning it. However, the point is that one must remain aware of their plots and harmfulness. As the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'He told you the truth, though he is a liar.' This matter can be adopted as a fundamental principle of learning.7. The jinn shaytan touches people's food. It consumes from it and spoils it.8. Ayat al-Kursi is a tremendous protection. Those who are able to practice it should not abandon this practice. If recited before sleeping at night, the reciter will remain free from all manner of harm, and no jinn shaytan will be able to overpower him.9. Ayat al-Kursi is this verse, verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah:اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُTranslation: Allah--there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Eternal Maintainer. Neither drowsiness nor sleep touches Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is there that can intercede with Him except with His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot encompass even a slight bit of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and preserving both does not burden Him. And He is the Exalted, the Supreme.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: It has come in the hadith--When a person remembers Allah (by saying Bismillah) upon entering the house and when taking food, Shaytan says, 'I have no food and no spending the night with you.' And when he does not remember Allah upon entering the house, Shaytan says, 'My spending the night will be with you.' And when he does not remember Allah at the time of eating, Shaytan says, 'Both spending the night and food have been arranged for me with you.' (Narrated by: Muslim, Hadith No. 2018)There is a specific du'a upon entering the house; recite it. If the du'a is not memorized, enter the house by at least saying Bismillah . . Likewise, at the time of eating, begin eating by saying Bismillah . .

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said,إذا تثاءب أحدكم فليمسك على فيه ، فإن الشيطان يدخلWhen one of you yawns, let him put his hand over his mouth to block it. For Shaytan enters when yawning. (Narrated by: Muslim and Abu Dawud)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: Evil jinn and devils roam in impure and unclean places. To stay safe from the possession of jinn, one must always stay away from impure, dirty places. Children must always be kept clean from garbage and filthy conditions.For example: it has come in a hadith narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam, the Noble Prophet (ﷺ) said, devils are present in these dirty places of urination and defecation. When any of you comes here, let him say,بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِTransliteration: Bismillaah, Allaahumma, innee a'oodhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khabaa'ithTranslation: In the name of Allah. O Allah! I seek refuge in You from male and female devils. [Narrated by: Sunan Abi Dawud, Sahih al-Bukhari: 142]Therefore, we understand from this hadith that jinn, ghosts, and devils reside in dirty places. Everyone should stay away from these dirty places.Shaykh al-Islam Imam Ibn Taymiyyah (rahimahullah) said, usually jinn reside in garbage, places of urination and defecation, dustbins, and graveyards. (Majmu' al-Fatawa)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, do not turn your houses into graveyards. Shaytan stays away from the house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited. (Sahih Muslim: 780)From this hadith, we learned the instruction to recite the Qur'an at home. Do not turn the house into a graveyard, the meaning of this is to recite the Qur'an at home. And when Surah Al-Baqarah is recited at home, Shaytan flees from the house. We know that Ayatul Kursi is in Surah Al-Baqarah itself.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: It has come in the hadith -The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade urinating in a hole. Qatadah (RA) was asked, what is the reason for this prohibition? He said, it is said that holes are the dwelling places of the jinn. (Narrated by: Sunan Abi Dawud)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: If a snake is seen in the house, do not kill it immediately, but utter a warning. Ask it to leave the house. After that, if it does not leave, then kill it.It has come in the hadith -Narrated from Abu as-Sa'ib, the freed slave of Hisham ibn Zuhrah, who said: I went to visit Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri (RA). I found him performing salah. I sat waiting for him to finish his salah. At that moment, I heard the sound of something moving under the bed in his room. I looked and saw a snake. I stood up to kill it. Abu Sa'eed (RA) gestured to me to sit down. When he finished the salah, he pointed toward a room in the house and said, "Do you see this room?" I said, "Yes, I see it."He said, "A young man used to live in this room. He was newly married. One day he joined the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of the Trench. Since he was a newly married young man, he asked permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying, 'O Messenger! I am newly married. Grant me permission to go to my wife.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission and said, 'Take your weapon with you. I fear an attack on you by Banu Qurayzah.' The young man set out toward his wife. Reaching the house, he found his wife standing outside between the two panels of the door. Seeing this situation hurt his sense of self-respect. He moved to strike her with a spear. His wife said, 'Do not hurry. First enter the house and see what is inside your house.' He entered the house and saw a snake coiled up lying on his bed."The young man struck the body of the snake with the spear. Then he brought it outside the house. The snake was writhing on the tip of the spear. And the young man then fell down dead. No one knows who died first, the young man or the snake? This incident was narrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said, "In Madinah, there are some jinn who have accepted Islam. If any of you sees any of them, give it a period of three days. If it is still seen after three days, then kill it. Because it is a shaytan." (Narrated by: Sahih Muslim, Chapter on Killing Snakes.)What we learned from this hadith is:1. The noble Companions taught others Islamic rulings and the Sunnah of the Noble Prophet (ﷺ) with utmost care.2. How compassionate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was toward his noble Companions and the Ummah, that during wartime, if someone asked for permission to go to his wife, he would grant it immediately. At times it was seen that he would ask his Companions on his own initiative, "How long has it been since you married? Who is in your house? I have given you leave, go home to your wife."3. If a snake is seen in the house, it should not be killed immediately. It might be a jinn. However, if upon seeing the snake or from its behavior and signs it is understood that it is not a jinn, but a snake, then killing it is not blameworthy. Look at the hadith under discussion: the snake was lying on the bed. If it were a snake, what need would it have on the bed? It would search for rats or insects.4. If such a suspicious snake is seen in the house, tell it aloud to leave the house. If it does not leave even after saying this for three days, then kill it.5. If a snake is seen in forests, jungles, mountains, or on the road, there is no reason to consider it a jinn. It must be killed. Only a house snake can be suspected of being a jinn. This is clearly stated in a sahih hadith.6. Because the snake was a jinn, it struck and killed the killer for the crime of killing it. But no one saw how the snake struck the young man.7. That the snake was a Muslim jinn is indicated by the words of the Messenger (ﷺ). It did not strike him initially, nor did it cause any harm to his wife.8. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Rahmatullil-'Alameen, or a mercy to all creation. Therefore, he showed mercy and compassion toward the jinn as well. Apart from this hadith, there are many other hadiths on this subject.9. "Because it is a shaytan"--the meaning of these words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is: it is not a jinn, it is wicked and harmful among animals. Kill it.10. Killing a jinn without reason is unjust.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, when any of you intends to have relations with his wife, if he says -بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ اَللَّهُمَّ جَنِّبْنَا الشَّيْطَانَ وَجَنِّبِ الشَّيْطَانَ مَا رَزَقْتَنَاTransliteration: Bismillaahi, Allaahumma, jannibnash-shaytaana wa jannibish-shaytaana maa razaqtanaaTranslation: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Shaytan away from us and keep Shaytan away from what You provide us.then if a child is born from this union, Shaytan will never be able to harm that child. (Narrated by: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said,When night spreads its wings or when you reach the evening, take care of your children. Restrain them from going outside. Because at that time, the devils disperse. When a part of the night has passed, you can let them go. And close the door. Remember the name of Allah. Know that Shaytan cannot open a closed door. (Narrated by: Sahih al-Bukhari)From this hadith, we learned the following matters:1. The instruction to take special care of children at evening time.2. Children must be told to come home before evening. At that time, forbid them from leaving the house.3. A while after evening, this fear no longer remains. At that time, there is no prohibition against children going out.4. The instruction to close the doors of the house at evening time.5. Another important piece of information learned from this hadith is that jinn or Shaytan cannot open the closed door of a house.6. The instruction is given to remember the name of Allah at the time of opening and closing the door.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Ways to Protect Oneself from Jinn Attacks and Harm
ruqyah_articles.text: If humans ask for anything from the jinn or seek their help, their insolence increases. They find encouragement to overpower humans. As Allah Rabbul-'Alameen says -وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمْ رَهَقًاTranslation: And indeed, there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they increased them in arrogance. (Surah Al-Jinn: 6)Many ojhas and fakirs are seen taking the help of jinn in matters of ta'weez and remedies; this is wrong.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Jinn can cause various types of illnesses and harm to humans, and are capable of harming their mental health, mood, body, wealth, status, business, relationships, and studies.The illnesses we will discuss here may occur due to the jinn exerting excessive power over humans or due to sorcerers. We will also discuss the treatment methods for these illnesses in the light of the Qur'an and Sunnah. These illnesses are as follows:1. Severe fear2. Mental and neurological illnesses (insanity, depression, anxiety, worry, epilepsy, waswasa, personality defects)3. Physical illnesses (illnesses that cannot be treated with man-made medicine, and for which there is no cure in medical science)4. Hallucinations or visual illusions5. Creating enmity and division by spreading hatred among people, such as between husband and wife, business partners, friends, and family members6. Gynaecological illnesses (infertility, excessive bleeding, irregular menstrual cycle, infections, etc.)7. Sexual problems (impotence, premature ejaculation)8. Damaging people's homes and material property (throwing household furniture around, throwing stones onto the roof of the house)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: There are two aspects to fearing the jinn. One is correct, and the other is not correct. The correct aspect is that some jinn can influence humans; through this, they make people hear various voices, show them things, and create a feeling within them that makes them feel as though someone is following them or pursuing them, and by creating this feeling, they scare people even in their own homes. To dispel this fear, one must regularly recite the Qur'an, recite the morning and evening adhkar, and follow a special routine for the person who is ill due to this fear.And the incorrect aspect is the deep panic rooted in people's minds regarding the jinn. There is no way to substantiate these fears from an Islamic perspective. Therefore, we will now outline why people fear the jinn so much and why they shudder in panic at the mere mention of the name of the jinn; only then can we grasp this problem and also remedy it.Reasons Why People Fear the Jinn1. First and foremost among the reasons for fear is people's ignorance of Tawhid. If there is a lack of knowledge regarding Tawhid in any place, ignorance spreads there. Myths prevail, and the wicked take control. Quack exorcists will find fertile ground to practice their false knowledge, and Shaytan will also assist them in their work. And because of this, people begin to believe that the jinn are capable of knowing the unseen, that they can bring benefit and ward off harm, whereas these attributes belong to Allah Ta'ala alone. For this reason, panic arises among people at the mere mention of the jinn.2. The widespread circulation of fabricated stories. People quite like listening to such stories, and after hearing them, they spread them to others at astonishing speed. These stories play a major role in easily creating fear among women, children, and weak-hearted people.3. Sorcerers also play a major role in spreading this fear, these stories, and myths among people.4. Due to negligence and failure to recite the adhkar prescribed in the Shari'ah, jinn often dwell within humans, and in many cases, people face harm from the jinn because of this.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Among the illnesses caused by jinn, mental and neurological illnesses are among the most prominent, such as insanity, depression, anxiety, etc. But it must certainly be mentioned that those who deny the role of the treatment methods for mental illnesses prescribed in medical science will not be doing the right thing. There is no contradiction or conflict between the treatment method prescribed in the Qur'an and the treatment method for mental illnesses prescribed in science.In hospitals and psychiatric clinics, there should also be a department for Qur'anic treatment, where the Qur'an will be recited for a person afflicted with mental illness. If the patient responds to the Qur'anic treatment in this department and begins to gradually improve, then gratitude must be expressed to Allah. And if they do not respond to it, there is no harm in that either, because Qur'anic treatment does not have any kind of side effects like the medicines and injections of conventional treatment methods.The interesting thing is, I once had a debate with a psychologist; he said: the one who attempts or practices Qur'anic treatment should first study psychology so that he acquires the capability to perform this kind of treatment. I said to him: what you are trying to say, I am trying to say the exact same thing to you. Qur'anic treatment does not have any negative side effects like your treatment. Since treating illness is your profession, add Qur'anic treatment to your treatment method as well.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: A number of physical illnesses also occur due to jinn. The number of such illnesses is many, but to put it briefly, when conventional treatment methods do not work for an illness, Qur'anic ruqyah should be recited over him in the hope that, if Allah wills, He may grant him healing.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: If jinn can subjugate or hypnotize people through magic (sihr), then with this power they are capable of making them see various unreal things or objects.For that reason, a man may see his wife as ugly and hideous, or a wife may see her husband in an ugly form due to the jinn; as a result, this ugly appearance of the partner can create an intense reaction in the mind of that husband or wife. In time, it can turn into severe irritation and depression--in reality. Although that husband or wife is not ugly at all. In this regard, Allah Ta'ala says:قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا ۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ ﴿٦٦﴾Translation: Musa said, "Rather, you throw." Then, because of their magic, it seemed to Musa that their ropes and staffs were moving about. (Ta-Ha 20:66)

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Humans have various types of pairs or bonds, such as husband and wife, or business partners, or friends; Shaytan has various tactics to spread hatred between these pairs or bonds. And through this plot of Shaytan, deep distance is created between loved ones over very trivial reasons, and each party cunningly takes a stand based on their own logic or explanation.When someone steps forward to resolve this kind of conflict, they find that each party believes they are in the right position. In this regard, it is narrated that Shaytan sends his troops in processions on missions to create this discord. Narrated from Jabir bin Abdullah (RA), he said, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying,"The throne of Shaytan is on the sea; sitting there, Shaytan sends his forces into human settlements to tempt people. And those among his forces who are most adept at creating problems or terrible discord hold the highest status in the eyes of Shaytan. One from among these devils of high status comes and says, 'I did not leave until I sowed discord between so-and-so and his wife.' Shaytan draws him close and says: 'You have done well.'" [Sahih Muslim, 66, 68]

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Jinn can also cause some other illnesses that only women suffer from, such as infertility, for which there is no medically explainable cause. When medical examinations are carried out, it is seen that neither the husband nor the wife has any problem, yet even so, the wife does not conceive.A friend of mine told me that he had been consulting a specialist doctor for four years; that doctor was quite satisfied with his physical condition, and that doctor told him, "I do not see any reason for your wife not conceiving. Both of them are 100% healthy." In the end, Allah Ta'ala also issued the decree that they should have a child, and my friend's wife conceived.However, it may be that there is a jinn in the uterus or ovaries, which destroys the sperm or ovum.In this case, there are also several medical symptoms; among these, we will mention a few here:1. Women feel a lot of pain in their back.2. Pain and infection in the uterine area.3. Irregular menstruation.4. Irregular bleeding.5. During intercourse, the wife feels extreme reluctance, and she participates in it only to please her husband.In addition, there are some other symptoms that may appear alongside these, such as headaches, nightmares, and numbness at peak moments, etc.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Types of Illnesses and Harm Caused by Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: Jinn play with household furniture and even burn many pieces of furniture; in this way, they can destroy people's homes. Such incidents actually happen, but they are very rare. I will mention some such real-life incidents here.[An article was published in the newspaper Al-Muslimoon (Issue No. 338, 15 Muharram 1412 AH / 26 July 1991 CE, p. 3) under the headline, 'Munif Harbi: Fire in My House Without Reason.']Munif Harbi is a Saudi citizen living in the Al-Naseem quarter of West Riyadh; regarding this fire, he says:Without any clear reason, fires broke out from every corner of my house. No one had ever seen such an incident before. And the civil defense forces could not provide any explanation for this fire either. As a result of this fire, his life was visibly on the verge of becoming like an unbearable, painful hell, but by the boundless grace of Almighty Allah, that did not happen.Similarly, an article was published in the newspaper Akhbar Al-Yom (Issue No. 2481, 20 Dhu al-Qi'dah 1412 AH / 23 May 1992, p. 14) under the headline, 'Fire Every Half Hour in a Doctor's House Right in Front of the Chief of the Girga Fire Brigade'.Major Rajab Sultan, chief of the fire brigade of the southern region of Sohag, stood stunned at the door of the forensic lab in a security forces office in Cairo, as if he were looking for something in the lab. He had just returned from Sohag after completing an astonishing mission, carrying in the bag he had with him some evidence of an astonishing fire that occurred in Sohag; these pieces of evidence were brought primarily to analyze what cause was involved behind the fire. But he was even more astonished when he saw that those pieces of evidence had vanished into thin air before he even stepped into the forensic lab; there was not even a trace of the evidence left.Major Rajab told that astonishing story in his own words; he said, last week Dr. Uthman Rifa'i, who works at Girga General Hospital, came to me and said that a fire had broken out in his house half an hour ago, and he had also notified the fire brigade to extinguish the fire and save his family. This message of his seemed rather surprising to me, yet I rushed to his house with my men and equipment to see if any clue about the fire could be found from the clothes in his home. That doctor told me that on the day of the incident, having returned from the hospital, he was having lunch with his wife and children, at which time a fire suddenly broke out in their bedroom.He called his neighbors; they came and helped extinguish the fire, and the fire was extinguished as well. But after that, every half hour, fires began to break out from all the wardrobes containing clothes in his home. A few minutes later, a wardrobe burst into flames right before my eyes; I was startled in sudden amazement. I extinguished the fire along with my men. Later, I discovered that the fire had started spontaneously from one of the clothes shelves.From inside that apartment, I contacted General Al-Sayyid Hasan using radio technology; Hasan is an assistant to the Minister of the Interior and the security chief of the Sohag region. I informed him about the fire here. He told me not to leave the apartment, and at the same time, he sent the police chief, a criminal investigation team, and forensic experts to assist me regarding this fire.Major Rajab Sultan further said that members of the security and fire forces crowded into that doctor's apartment; they thoroughly examined every inch of the apartment and tried to find the cause of the fire. They tried to pose a possibility that perhaps some powder was kept somewhere in the house that triggered the fire, but even after much investigation, they found no such possibility. Rather, right in front of these security and fire forces, fire broke out in the apartment once again; everywhere in the apartment, from the children's bedroom to the household furniture, even clothes soaked for washing caught fire. Seeing this scene, the members of the fire brigade rushed forward with their equipment to extinguish the fire, while the doctor's family members and children were screaming in panic. Members of the security and fire forces worked continuously on this fire until the following day. But they could not find any cause or source of this fire that ignited every half hour.The security chief ordered some members of the fire brigade to stay in that apartment so that they could protect the doctor's family from the fire. And he instructed me to go on a special mission to Cairo the next morning. At the time of departure, he also told me to take evidence in a bag from the fire-burned clothes of the apartment to test in the forensic lab, so that a scientific explanation of this fire could be found through it. But right upon arriving at the door of the forensic lab, I discovered that those fire samples I had brought in my bag had vanished into thin air. I could not even know when and how this incident happened.Later, Major Rajab Sultan returned to Sohag again to collect fresh evidence. Even then he was stunned in bewilderment, asking himself: despite my presence as the fire brigade chief, how did this fire break out there? How can the doctor's family be protected from the clutches of this strange fire? Will we need the assistance of any other fire brigade to make this mission successful?The second story is narrated by Ibn al-Qayyim (rahimahullah) in his book Al-Wabil al-Sayyib (pp. 176-177), where it is recorded that Abu an-Nadr al-Hashim bin al-Qasim said, 'A stone was thrown at me targeting my house, and immediately afterward a voice was heard, "O Abu an-Nadr! Come out of your house."' He said, I fell into deep distress over this incident. So, describing this incident, I wrote a letter to Ibn Idris al-Muharibi and Abu Usamah in Kufa. Al-Muharibi wrote in reply to my letter: There was a dry well in Madinah. Once a caravan came and pitched tents near this well. The locals came and informed them about the dry well. Hearing this, the people of the caravan asked the locals for a bucket of water.Afterward, they poured the bucket of water into the well saying the following words. Instantly, fire flared up from within the well and was extinguished right at the mouth of the well. The words they spoke while pouring the water were: In the name of Allah Ta'ala, the Most Merciful; we are in the protection of Allah Ta'ala, to Whom nothing is impossible, and through the greatness of Allah which can never be overcome, and through the boundless power of Allah, we, the powerful ones too, pray to Him for protection.By the Beautiful Names of Allah, I seek refuge from the hand of Shaytan, I seek refuge from the evil of humans and jinn, and I also seek refuge from those devils who are visible and invisible, who appear by night and disappear by day, and who disappear by night and appear by day; I seek refuge from those devils that He has created, and I also seek refuge from all forms of evil of Iblis and his army. And I also seek refuge from the evil of those beasts whose forelock (control) is in Your hand. I also seek refuge with Allah from those matters from which Musa, Isa, and Ibrahim (AS) as well sought refuge (An-Najm: 53:37), and I seek refuge from all those evils that He has created, from the evil of Shaytan and his army, and from all other harmful evil things. I seek refuge with Allah Almighty, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, from the evil of the accursed Shaytan. I begin in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا ﴿١﴾ فَالزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْرًا ﴿٢﴾ فَالتَّالِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا ﴿٣﴾ إِنَّ إِلَٰهَكُمْ لَوَاحِدٌ ﴿٤﴾ رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ الْمَشَارِقِ ﴿٥﴾ إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ ﴿٦﴾ وَحِفْظًا مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ ﴿٧﴾ لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ ﴿٨﴾ دُحُورًا ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ ﴿٩﴾ إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ الْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ ﴿١٠﴾Translation: By the angels lined up in rows, then those who drive (the clouds) smoothly, and those who recite the Reminder (the Heavenly Book); indeed, your God is One; Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the sunrises. Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the beauty of the stars, and protected it from every rebellious devil. They cannot listen to the higher realm, because they are pelted from every side (with meteors) to drive them away, and for them is a perpetual punishment. Except one who snatches something by stealth, then a burning meteor pursues him. (Surah As-Saffat 37:1-10)Abu al-Nadr said: Then I took a bucket of water and recited the above du'a over it, then I sprinkled this water around the house. At this, they (the jinn) cried out at me, saying: "You have burned us! We will not bother you anymore." [Al-Wabil al-Sayyib - Ibn al-Qayyim 176-177]In one of his speeches, Shaykh Ali bin Musharraf al-Umari recounted an incident of a fire: a fire broke out without reason in a house in a place called Hadban near Madinah, but after extinguishing the fire, it flared up again, and the fire brigade could not discover any cause for this fire. After Shaykh Mannai arrived at that place, he found out the cause; he sat in that place and recited the Qur'an, and then the jinn who caused this fire and put the residents of the house in distress. He expelled them.Although it is possible for such incidents to occur, it is very rare. We must be sure whether this is truly the work of jinn or. not, because liars and quack exorcists fabricate countless such stories to serve their own interests. One such incident was narrated by Shaykh Yasin Ahmad Eid. He said:"A short time ago, a man passed away; at the time of death, he left behind a beautiful house. The house was somewhat separate or. isolated from other houses. The house was quite large, had many rooms, and was well-furnished.In the courtyard of the house was a pool made of marble stone. Around it were several statues of various shapes and colors, through whose mouths water also flowed.The man had no children to be his heirs; for that reason, after his death, the house became vacant. In the hope of getting a high price, his relatives agreed to sell the house, but as soon as they got ready and began frantic preparations to sell the house, right then a rumor spread that the house had been occupied by jinn and an 'ifrit was living inside.This rumor continued to spread, eventually becoming the main topic of discussion in the city, the talk of the town. This rumor began to be discussed in evening chat sessions. If anyone disagreed with it and went to that house at night to verify the truth, in the morning he would return with the idea that the house was indeed occupied by jinn.As a result, no one was interested in buying that house anymore; those who were the heirs also became quite frustrated and panicked thinking of its bad outcome, especially when buyers offered one-fourth of the price for the house, they realized that the situation was not very good. Seeing no other way, the heirs were almost about to sell the house; in the meantime, a brave young man came forward upon hearing news of the house, having heard everything about this house from people. He had no fear regarding jinn or an 'ifrit, nor did he even pay any heed to them. He made a vow to the people that he would drive the jinn away from that house and catch the 'ifrit or expel it in exchange for money. The heirs agreed to his proposal, and they paid him half of the agreed remuneration in advance.In the morning, the young man set out toward that house taking a pistol with him. After reaching the house, he rested for a while, and at one point, having extinguished the candle, fell asleep. After a while, he sensed that someone was pulling the blanket away from him; the young man immediately gripped the blanket with all his strength and said: "Who is pulling my blanket?" Then a voice called out, "I am an 'ifrit, and I must take this blanket, otherwise I will take up residence in your body." As soon as the young man let go of the blanket, that man tumbled down behind him.The young man got up, sat on that 'ifrit's chest, pointed a pistol to his head, and said: "Tell me, who are you?". The 'ifrit became very frightened and said: "Release me, I will tell you who I really am." The young man said: "Speak, O 'ifrit!" He said: "I am neither an 'ifrit nor a jinn; I am a human being just like you. There is only one difference between us: I look very black and ugly." After hearing this, the young man released him and lit the candle to see who the man really was. In the candlelight, he saw a naked black man.The young man said: "Tell me, O black man! Why did you come. here?" The man said: Necessity has brought me here, because. I am very poor, have no income, have a huge family at home, and there is no one else to look after them except me. In this situation, I approached a man for work. That man told me to come and stay in this house every night. That man told me that if anyone tried to come toward this house, then I should first I. clap and strike the wall.But even after that, if it is seen that the person is very brave and is not paying any heed to these frightening noises, then I should turn on the water taps so that water starts flowing out of the mouths of the statues, then I should quickly go up to the roof and shout in different voices to scare him. After that, he told me to keep this matter secret. After hearing this incident, the young man took the man with him and handed him over to the heirs of the house. He disclosed everything to them, and in this way it became clear that the man who had hired this black man wanted to buy the house at a very cheap price.

ruqyah_articles.subcategory: Treatment of People's Irrational Fear of Jinn
ruqyah_articles.text: The fundamental basis of all acts of worship, reviving various practices or customs of Islam, and teaching. people that all good and evil are in the hands of Allah alone, is to call people to Tawhid.Without the will of Allah, no creation--no matter how great it may be--can bring benefit or harm to anyone; it does not possess this power. The power to do good or cause harm to anyone is solely in the hands of Allah Almighty and All-Powerful.Allah Almighty says:قُل لَّا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ۗTranslation: Say, 'I possess not for myself any harm or benefit, except what Allah wills.'
